Director's Corner
It is a privilege and honour for me to have led the NIT Jamshedpur as a Director of the Institution. NIT Jamshedpur has a rich legacy of more than sixty dedicated years of service to the nation and its pride of Jharkhand.  NIT Jamshedpur takes extreme pride in the fact that it has been occupying a unique position in imparting technological education to Indian youth. Since its inception, the institute has had a vision to provide quality technical education and to facilitate scientific and technological research, coupled with a mission to develop human potential to its zenith with excellence in teaching and high quality research.
Read More
Our Vision
To be one of the premier technical institutions for its academic excellence and innovative research to meet the future needs of the society.
Our Mission
1. To build conducive environment for learning and creativity.
2. To train students to become technically competent professionals and socially responsible citizens.
3. To develop innovative products and technologies for the betterment of the society.

TAP @ NIT JSR
The Training & Placement Cell, NIT Jamshedpur, facilitates the process of placement of students passing out from the institute, besides collaborating with leading organizations and institutes in setting up internship and training programs for students. The office liaises with various industrial establishments, corporate houses, etc, which conduct campus interviews and select Graduate, Post-Graduate and PhD students from all disciplines. The Training & Placement Cell provides the infra-structural facilities to conduct group discussions, tests, and interviews, besides catering to other logistics. The office interacts with many industries in the country, of which nearly 100+ companies visit the campus to hold campus interviews. The industries which approach the institute come under the purview of Core Engineering industries, IT & IT enabled services, Manufacturing Industries, Consultancy Firms, Finance Companies, Management Organisations and R&D laboratories.
The placement season runs through the course of the year. Pre-Placement Talks are also conducted in this regard as per mutual convenience. Job offers, dates of interviews, selection of candidates, etc., are announced through the Training & Placement Cell. The Placement Office is assisted by a committee comprising representatives of students from the Graduate, Post-Graduate and PhD streams. The committee evolves a broad policy framework every year besides a set of inviolable rules. Student members are closely co-opted in implementing these policy decisions.

Message
At NIT Jamshedpur, we take immense pride in the accomplishments and contributions of our alumni, who continue to excel and lead in various fields across the globe. This page is dedicated to celebrating the enduring bond between the institute and its graduates, while also serving as a bridge to connect past, present, and future generations of the NIT Jamshedpur community.
Whether you are an alumnus reflecting on your journey, a current student seeking inspiration, or a faculty member looking to engage with former students, this platform is your gateway to a vibrant network of professionals and leaders. Here, you can explore alumni success stories, reconnect with old friends, and discover opportunities for mentorship, collaboration, and growth.
Our goal is to foster a community where knowledge, experience, and support are shared freely, enriching the lives of all who are part of the NIT Jamshedpur family. We invite you to stay connected, participate in events, and contribute to the ongoing legacy of our institution.
Thank you for being a part of this remarkable journey. Together, we continue to shape the future with the same spirit of innovation, excellence, and camaraderie that defines NIT Jamshedpur.

Prof. Goutam Sutradhar
Director
Prof. (Dr.) Goutam Sutradhar currently the Director at the National Institute of Technology, Jamshedpur, since 12th May 2023. Before this, he served as the Director of NIT Manipur for a full term of five years. He completed his Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering from Jalpaiguri Government Engineering College, West Bengal in 1984. He subsequently earned his Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering with a specialization in Foundry Technology from IIT Kharagpur in 1986. He completed his Ph.D. in Engineering from Birla Institute of Technology (BIT) Mesra, Ranchi. After working for five years in Hindustan Motors Limited and Indian Railways, he joined as a faculty member at the National Institute of Foundry & Forge Technology, Ranchi, Jharkhand in 1991. He later served at Serampore Textile College, West Bengal and Kalyani Government Engineering College, West Bengal for about ten years before joining Jadavpur University, Kolkata, as a Professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering in 2005. He has supervised more than 20 M.Tech thesis and 21 Ph.D. students in the field of Metal Matrix Composites, Polymer Matrix Composites, Development of Environment-friendly Materials, Synthesis of Forged Powder Metallurgy Components, and Metal Casting Processes. He has supervised many research projects sponsored by AICTE, New Delhi; CSIR, New Delhi; UGC, New Delhi; DST, New Delhi. He has authored two books, namely "Design and Manufacturing: An Integrated Approach" published by Oxford & IBH, and "Foundry Process Design" published by New Age Publishers, New Delhi. He has published over 125 technical papers in referred journals of national and international importance and presented more than 50 technical papers at national and international conferences.

Message From the Director
Greetings from the Director!
It is a privilege and honour for me to have led the NIT Jamshedpur as a Director of the Institution. NIT Jamshedpur has a rich legacy of more than sixty dedicated years of service to the nation and its pride of Jharkhand. NIT Jamshedpur takes extreme pride in the fact that it has been occupying a unique position in imparting technological education to Indian youth. Since its inception, the institute has had a vision to provide quality technical education and to facilitate scientific and technological research, coupled with a mission to develop human potential to its zenith with excellence in teaching and high quality research. In consonance with its vision, the institute has been contributing substantially to our country's technological power. NIT Jamshedpur emphasizes the need to promote entrepreneurship by introducing entrepreneurial spirit and start up as a part of the curriculum. It is fast emerging as a global knowledge centre for quality research and teaching through cross disciplinary, innovative and dynamic approaches. It is indeed a pleasure in mentioning that institute is leading active research collaborations and have established vital links with many repreted institution industry, business and government agencies. The Institute is aiming to develop 21th century skills and competencies supported by different learning frameworks and Industry supported by a one semester internship program for undergraduate and postgraduate students.  As a result year after year, with its exemplary placement record, NIT Jamshedpur has reinforced its brand image as a leading technical institution. I on the behalf of all stakeholders, would like to call everyone to work on converged ideas to achieve the most deserved position at national and international levels. Institutes will have significant contributions in different flagship programs of our country like make in India, Start up India, Standup India .
With best regards

Choudhary 9431 161 850 Monitoring Committee: A monitoring Committee is also entrusted with the responsibility of overseeing the implementation of the verdict, and functioning of various Anti-ragging committees. Counselling of freshers and senoirs: A Team Comprising of Dean (SW), Chief warden , Proctor ,Co-ordinator (Training and placement) will coordinate this activity. Affidavit & undertakings from the students and parent: Each student of the the institute ,his/her parents and each guardian are required to submit an Affidavit (as per the guidelines of the UGC Regulations) and a set of Undertakings (as per the directives of supreme court of India) to prevent and control ragging. Complaint boxes: Complaint Boxes in all hostels in general and hostels C & D in particular are kept for reporting the incidence of ragging, if any.These boxes are also installed at two places in the institute building,Library & Computer Centre. Dean(SA) will ensure that the complaint boxes are also kept in the hostels where 1st year students are accommodated. Information to Local Administration & Police station: The Local administration and the police station of the area(RIT police station)have been informed and requested to keep constant vigil/patrol around first year hostels particularly to prevent any untoward incidence/ragging. The Local administration have been requested to intensify the regular patrolling in the NIT campus area in view of the presence of new students and disturbance caused by the local elements. About Us
National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur,earlier known as Regional Institute of Technology was established on 15th August 1960 as a joint venture of Government of India and the Government of Bihar in the chain of REC's (Regional Engineering College) in India with the aim to generate technical graduates of highest standards who could provide technological leadership to the region. It was among the first eight Regional Engineering Colleges (RECs) established as part of the Second Five-Year Plan (1956 - 1961). This was the only REC in the country which was named as RIT (Regional Institute of Technology). Therefore RIT Jamshedpur was actually the REC of undivided Bihar & Jharkhand. The foundation stone of RIT (REC) Jamshedpur was laid by Dr. Srikrishna Sinha, the then chief minister of Bihar , with the aim of nurturing talent and setting high standards of education and excellence. On 27th December 2002, in the line of all other RECs of India, RIT Jamshedpur (may be read as REC Jamshedpur too) was converted to National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur with the status of a Deemed University as per the decision of Govt. of India. The Institute is fully funded and governed by the Ministry of Education (MoE), Government of India since 1st April, 2003. On 15 August 2007, NIT Jamshedpur was given the status of the Institute of National Importance through an Act of the Parliament known as the NIT Act. The Institute has 11 departments including engineering, science and humanities. The Institute, with 200 faculty, 4000 students, 150 administrative and supporting staff, is a self-contained campus. It is located on the outskirts of Jamshedpur on 341.3 acres of sprawling, rolling hilly, wooded land. It combines natural beauty of countryside with urban glamour of an industrial area. The flowing river and picturesque backdrop of low hills on one side and large tracks of forest on the other make the campus an ideal place for higher learning and research. It has been growing from strength to strength ever since it was established in 1960. Situated in the heart of the rich mineral and industrial belt of Jharkhand State, the campus encompasses the Main building, the Library, the Computer Center, 13 hostels (7 Boys hostels, 6 Girls hostels), 2 hostels Under-Construction, staff quarters, Guest House, a Students Gymkhana, a Post-office , a branch of State Bank of India, two ATMs, central store and a dispensary. The hostels and departments are connected with high speed wireless LAN. The institute maintains courts for basketball, volleyball, badminton and tennis. Apart from this, it also has cricket, hockey and football grounds. The institute is poised for bright and promising future. The courses have been completely restructured and prepared as per the needs of society and industries. There is refreshing development on every front. The institute has achieved impressive placement for its students, with top industrial houses and software companies recruiting the students in large numbers.
Location
NIT Jamshedpur is situated in the western part of the city Jamshedpur , which is in the southern end of the state of Jharkhand and is bordered by the states of Orissa and West Bengal. It is just far enough to ensure that the city with its noise is too distant to distract and just near enough to guarantee that all city facilities are immediately available. The institute is strategically located with the unique advantage of being surrounded by giant and medium scale industries like Tata-Steel, Telco, Indian Steel Wire Products, Tata Tubes, Tinplate Company, Tata Timken etc. and reputed Institutes like the National Metallurgical Laboratory, Xavier Labour Relations Institute and National Institute of Foundry and Forge Technology, Ranchi. History
NIT, Jamshedpur was formally inaugurated on 15th August 1960 at Adityapur, Jamshedpur by Dr. Srikrishna Sinha, the then and also the first Chief Minister of Bihar and the first Chairman of the Board of Governors of RIT, Jamshedpur. His eloquent speech highlighted the dreams and aspirations to be nurtured by the institute to achieve excellence in higher technical education, research and development. This inaugural address was termed 'the first lecture' in Humanities by the founder Principal Dr. R. P. Verma. It is noteworthy that both the founder Chairman and the founder Principal happened to be freedom fighters. Their nationalistic fervour and passion for progress set the college moving on the right path towards technological development. The historical day at RIT, Jamshedpur was 27th December, 2002 when it was formally upgraded to National Institute of Technology, Jamshedpur with the Deemed University status. R.I.T., Jamshedpur started off by offering undergraduate courses in four branches (viz Civil, Electrical, Mechanical and Metallurgy) of Engineering in 1960. The institute also offers M.Tech, Ph. D., Non-Formal B. Sc. Engineering Programme and MCA programmes.

How to Reach Jamshedpur
Jamshedpur is the first well-planned industrial city of India, founded by the late Jamshedji Nusserwanji Tata and ranks 28th among the 35 million-plus cities and is also the 31st urban agglomeration in India according to the census 2001. Located in the East Singhbhum district of Jharkhand on the Chota Nagpur plateau, it is the district headquarters and is surrounded by the beautiful Dalma Hills. The rivers Subarnarekha and Kharkai border the North and West of the city, respectively. The institute is located in Adityapur town of the district which is at the border of Saraikela-Kharswan district and East Singhbhum district. Adityapur is a highly industrialized town having hundreds of small and medium scale industries.
Airways
Birsa Munda Airport, Ranchi, Jharkhand
is connected with Jamshedpur through NH-33 via Chandil and Bundu. Road distance is about 140 KM between the two cities. You may add about 15 KM more to this distance as the Airport is about 5 KM from Ranchi city and NIT Jamshedpur is about 10 KM from the Jamshedpur bus-stand. Numerous bus services are available between Ranchi and Jamshedpur. Ranchi is also connected with Jamshedpur by rail-route distance is 167 KM by train but the bus route is convenient.
Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Domestic & International Airport, Kolkata.
It is an international airport located in Kolkata, West Bengal, India. It is 260km away from Jamshedpur. The best way of travelling between Jamshedpur and Kolkata is by train. The train journey takes 4 - 5 hours. By road it takes about 6 hours.
Railways
The railway station of Jamshedpur is known as Tatanagar Junction. Tatanagar (Jamshedpur) is an important railway junction & a model station on the South Eastern Railway and is the most important railway junction of the state as it is connected directly to all the major cities of India, viz., Kolkata, Mumbai, Delhi, Chennai, Bangalore, Ahmedabad, Amritsar, Raipur, Patna, Nagpur, Kanpur, Ranchi, Pune, Jammu, Vishakapatnam, Guwahati, Bhubaneshwar etc.
Tatanagar Junction is 135 KM from Kharagpur and 250 KM from Howrah (Kolkata) by train route. It is well connected to Kharagpur and Howrah Junctions through over a dozen of super-fast/express/local trains. Jamshedpur is well connected to other parts of India through national and state highways. The major highways are:
National Highway 33 (NH 33) touches the city and joins the NH32, which connects Kolkata with Delhi.
National Highway 32 (NH 32) connects Jamshedpur to Govindpur via Dhanbad.
Direction to reach the Institute from Tatanagar railway station and Jamshedpur main Bus Stand(Sakchi)
The Institute’s Administrative Building is
9.5 KM from Jamshedpur main bus stand at Mango, 8.5 KM from Tatanagar railway station and only 2 KM from Adityapur railway station which is a small station.
Distance between Adityapur railway station and Tatanagar Jn is 4 KM. While coming from Howrah side, Tatanagar Jn comes before Adityapur station, and while coming from Mumbai/ Bilaspur/ Durg/ Rourkela/ Patna/ Asansol side, Adityapur station comes before Tatanagar Jn. All local trains and few express trains stop at Adityapur station. Therefore, while coming from Mumbai/ Nagpur/ Bilaspur/ Durg/ Rourkela/ Patna/ Asansol side, one should get down if the train stops at Adityapur station and reserve an auto-rickshaw or taxi (fare Rs 60/- as in Jun 2013) for the institute. Frequent local transports are available from Jamshedpur main Bus stand, Mango and Tatanagar Junction on reserved as well as shared basis. From Tatanagar railway station you must go to Bistupur. From Jamshedpur main bus stand, you must go to Sakchi and then Bistupur . From Bistupur you should take an auto to Adityapur. At Adityapur you must get down near the All India Radio Building.It is better to reserve an auto to the Institute campus from there. If you don’t reserve an auto, you have to turn left towards the railway under-bridge to travel along the NIT road to reach the Institute which is located at Adityapur-2. The Institute Administrative Building is 3.5 KM from the All India Radio located at Adityapur-1. There is an alternative route (about 0.5 KM longer than the above mentioned route via railway over-bridge and NIT road) to the institute campus via NIT MORE (also pronounced as “mod”) from Adityapur-Kandra main road. While coming from Bistupur side, in stead of turning left near All India Radio Building at Adityapur-1, one may go ahead straight and take left turn at NIT MORE which is about 2 KM from All India Radio Building. The institute administrative building is about 2 KM from NIT MORE. On reserved basis you may take an auto from any corner of the city to the Institute premises. For people who are coming here for first time,it is recommended to reserve an auto. The fare is Rs. 150 from Main bus stand or main railway station to the main campus.
Regular bus services are available from Jamshedpur to Ranchi (131 km), Patna, Gaya, Kolkata (300 km) via Baharagora, Hazaribagh, Puri, Bhubaneshwar, Asansol, Bokaro, Dhanbad etc. However, Roadways travel on Kolkata-Kharagpur-Jamshedpur route is not recommended as train route is much better (faster, cheaper, safe and comfortable).

About
The Department of Civil Engineering of National Institute of Technology (formerly Regional Institute of Technology) Jamshedpur was started since the inception of the institute itself in 1960. This core department has sanctioned strength of 33 (thirty-three) faculty members with flexible faculty structure. The department is running UG course for B. Tech. (Hons) degree in Civil Engineering and PG courses as M. Tech. degree in the streams of Structural Engineering, Geotechnical Engineering and Water Resource Engineering as well as Ph. D. program in various streams of Civil Engineering. The department has well qualified and experienced faculty members. Apart from teaching and research, all faculty members are actively involved in administrative woks and other extracurricular activities for all round development of the Institute. Faculty members of the department are also undertaking design, testing & consultancy works for various organizations leading to resource generation for the Institute.
Vision
To become the best department for the research, academic and consultancy with the vigorous participation of faculty, research scholars and students and produce smart solutions with ethics and morals in the field of civil engineering for the benefit of society and industry.
Mission
To develop modern laboratories, centre of excellence and advanced computational facilities. To conduct research in all fields of civil engineering and interdisciplinary areas. To motivate research scholars and students towards best professional practices. To make graduating students exposed to industry and R & D organizations to get better opportunities. To offer educational programmes that imparts inventive knowledge with high levels of ethical and human values.

About
Department of Chemistry, National Institute of Technology, Jamshedpur was originally founded as Regional Institute of Technology in 11260 with the aim of nurturing talent and setting high standards of education and excellence. The Department offers instruction in General Chemistry and Engineering Chemistry to the students in different branches of Engineering students at B.Tech level. The Department started Post Graduate Programme (M.Tech) in Surface Science and Engineering since 1982.The department is equipped with various instruments. Besides teaching, the highly qualified and energetic faculty members of the Department have contributed a lot to elevate the prestige of the institute through their research activities of both basic and applied areas of chemistry.
Vision
To create the Department of Chemistry as a centre of excellence in science and technology through enhanced collaboration between Industries and academia and serving the country. Building world class research facility to train young minds through extensive research curriculum. To provide a pool of bright scientists for advanced scientific endeavour of our country.
Mission
To provide good fundamental concept of Chemistry applied to the Engineering field. To introduce the importance of Chemistry in industry as well as in research field. To study the importance of chemicals, chemical reactions and physical phenomena, synthesis in higher study of Engineering.

About
Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering was started in 1989. The department covers a host of subjects inclusive of Electronic Circuits, Microprocessor, Digital signal processing, Analog communication, Digital communication, Mobile communication, VLSI, Embedded systems, Instrumentation etc. The department has laboratories catering to all the subjects of studies. There are five research scholars working in different specializations under the groups of Communication Engineering, VLSI and Embedded systems, Signal Processing, Instrumentation and Soft computing. The Department has highly motivated faculty pool to cater our needs.
Vision
Global Knowledge Hub Excellence in technical and interdisciplinary domain Amalgam of research and entrepreneurship in pursuit of Make in India drive Beckoning pillar for digital India
Mission
Imparting total quality education to develop next generation professional scholar, fit for globally competitive environment. Value creation through economic, social, and environmental development using original ideas through discovery, inquiry, innovation, research, transformational scholarship, and creative activities. Dramatic increase in product oriented research for establishing a self-sustaining and wealth creating centre by involving the interaction between committed, diverse faculty, staff, students and community, to serve the societal needs of the State of Jharkhand, India and ultimately, the world.

About
When the institute was established in 1960 as Regional Institute of Technology, the Department came into being as Humanities Department and was fashioned on the lines of the Department of Humanities and Social Sciences at IITs. The Department was engaged in the teaching of English, Philosophy, Psychology, Political Science and Economics to B.Sc. (Engg.) students. In 2014, the Department was upgraded to the Department of Humanities, Social Sciences and Management. The department is currently engaged in teaching English for Communication, Introduction to Soft Skills, Organizational Behaviour and Industrial Psychology, Industrial Economics and Accountancy, Management Information System courses to B Tech (Hons.) students and Technical Communication to M.Tech,Communication kills to M.Sc,Financial Management ,Drag Behaviour and Management to MCA and Electives(principles of eco entrepreneurship Development). The faculty members of the department are also training students in the area of oral and written communication skills for placement purposes. The department plans to start a two year full time, post graduate MBA programme in near future.
Vision
To contribute to the emergence of NIT Jamshedpur as a world class institution, producing highly skilled engineers who are finest specimens of technology at its best merging aesthetics with human values and social responsibility to make this world a better place.
Mission
To contribute to the holistic development of the personality of the students so as to enable them to successfully meet their professional as well as societal challenges and to inculcate essential human values in them and also to make them sensitive to the concerns of environment.

About
The Department of Mechanical Engineering is one of the oldest (started in 1960) and the largest department in terms of faculty, students and activities. The Department offers B.Tech (Hons.) in Mechanical Engineering, M.Tech in Computer Integrated Design & Manufacturing (CIDM), M.Tech in Thermal Engineering (TE) and M.Tech in Energy System (ES). Department is also running PhD Program in various research areas in the Mechanical Engineering. It also offers part time PhD program, mainly meant for those employed in industries and academic institutions. The department is having highly qualified and experienced faculty in all streams of Mechanical Engineering. An interactive relationship is maintained between the students and staff which enables the students to develop a sound foundation in the stream in a conduciven environment.
Vision
To be a centre for imparting world class education in the field of Mechanical Engineering and conduct extensive and quality research and to propel innovations for the betterment of society.
Mission
To train young minds and to equip them with the best possible technical knowledge to meet the current and future demands of the industry, academic & research. To create infrastructure, motivation and culture for the state of the art research work in the area of Mechanical Engineering. To enhance the research and teaching by interaction and development of relation with industry, R&D organization and academic institutions. To develop an energetic environment for excellence, creativity and perfection.

About
The Department of Physics at the National Institute of Technology, Jamshedpur, was formed in 1960. Since its inception, the department has been recognized all over the country for its excellence. The department has consistently produced quality professionals in the field of physics and strived for excellence in research and development. The Department has at present 9 faculty members including DST-Inspire Faculty and 11 research scholars engaged in doctoral research.The Department actively participates in front-line research in several major areas of Physics including Solar Energy, Nuclear scattering and Supersymmetry, Mathematical Physics, Holography and holographic optical element, Speckle Meterology, Condensed Matter Physics, Plasma Physics, Computational Physics and Spectroscopy.At present department offer 2 years Master of Science (Physics) Programme as well as a Ph.D. Programme with specialization in various major areas of Physics. The Department also participates in teaching Engineering Physics to B.Tech. (Hons.) students of all the disciplines namely- Civil Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Electrical and Electronics Engineering, Electronics and Communication Engineering, Production and Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering and Metallurgical & Materials Engineering of the Institute. Our M.Sc. students are ranking good in national level competitive exams like CSIR-NET, GATE, JEST as well as in the INSPIRE Fellow scheme offered by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), India.
Vision
Quality education in physics and produce highly technically trained human resources of world class. Promote research and development in applied physics in the emerging and thrust areas and attainment of academic excellence. Provide greater understanding of the nature of physical science, an appreciation of physics in everyday life, and technical expertise. Excellence in technical and multidisciplinary domain.
Mission
To provide quality education, understanding in physics and development of experimental skills to produce well prepared graduates. To provide dynamic, forward looking and responsive to global technological development by imparting excellent technical education.

About
The Department of Production & Industrial Engineering was started in year 1988 with the name of “Production Engineering & Management”. The name of this department was changed to Production & Industrial Engineering in the year 2007. The department was accredited by NBA in 2009. This core department has a sanctioned strength of 16 (Sixteen) faculty members with flexible faculty structure. Presently, there are 02 Professor, 03 Associate professors and 08 Assistant Professors. Every faculty member has received doctorate degree in different research areas. The department is running a UG course for B. Tech. (Hons.) degree in Production and industrial Engineering and a PG course in Manufacturing Systems Engineering as well as Ph. D. program in various streams of Production and Industrial Engineering. The Department is currently developing different engineering laboratories like CAD/CAM Lab., Advanced Manufacturing and Flexible manufacturing systems Lab., Non- Traditional Manufacturing lab, and Industrial Engineering & Ergonomics lab and Central workshop. Time to time curricula/syllabus is upgraded as per the market and technology requirement. The department has also proposed to start a new PG course in Production Management which will cater to the current industrial need.
Vision
To produce engineers and researchers with excellent technical knowledge, research acumen, leadership skills and ethical responsibility.
Mission
To educate B. Tech., M. Tech and Ph. D students with fundamental knowledge in concerned subjects, and to update them with the state-of-the-art in the field. To develop and maintain laboratories which cater to the needs of the students Quest for inter-disciplinary research. To promote academia-industry collaboration

Dr Abhijit  Dey
Assistant Professor
Mechanical Engineering
Dr. Abhijit Dey is an accomplished academic and
    researcher, currently serving as an Assistant Professor in the Department of
    Mechanical Engineering at the National Institute of Technology (NIT)
    Jamshedpur, India. With over seven years of teaching and research experience,
    Dr. Dey has previously been associated with NIT Srinagar, NIT Silchar, and MITS
    Madanapalle in Andhra Pradesh, where he made significant contributions to
    advancing knowledge in mechanical engineering. Dr. Dey's research expertise
    lies in the development of
Ceramic Matrix Composites (CMCs)
and the machinability of
Metal Matrix Nano-Composites (MMCs)
and
CMC
s, Mechanical, Nano-Mechanical and Tribological behavior of the Composites and alloys focusing on enhancing their performance in extreme conditions. His
    innovative work in
Gradient and Nano-Layered coatings
for
    advanced industrial applications has positioned him at the forefront of
    materials science. These cutting-edge solutions address critical challenges in
    sectors such as aerospace, defense, and biomedical engineering. Throughout his
    career, Dr. Dey has demonstrated a commitment to excellence in both teaching
    and research. His contributions include mentoring students, publishing
    impactful research, and fostering collaborations with leading institutions to
    drive innovations in surface engineering and composite materials. Dr. Dey's
    dedication to advancing the field of mechanical engineering is reflected in his
    ongoing efforts to explore new materials and technologies, pushing the
    boundaries of what is possible in modern engineering applications. His work not
    only enhances industrial performance but also inspires the next generation of
    engineers and researchers.

Dr Abhishek Majhi
Assistant Professor
Department of Physics
My PhD work (SINP Kolkata, 2009-14) was related to aspects of black holes in loop quantum gravity. My postdoc research works (IISER TVM, IMSc Chennai, UNAM Mexico City [2014-18]) were partly a continuation of my PhD work and largely a diversification on different aspects related to the interface of gravitational and quantum physics. During my tenure as an INSPIRE Faculty in ISI Kolkata (2018-23), the formulation of
a non-singular (asymptotically safe) theory of two body gravitational interaction happened through me while I was working on the gravitational singularity problem (considered as an open problem in theoretical physics, otherwise). In an accompanying work, a similar construction was shown for the electrostatic two body interaction which was, however, mainly focused on the role of human choice in the `proof' of the first Maxwell equation. These works were founded upon a diversified research concerning the foundations and philosophy of mathematical science, which made me deconstruct the very language of science and its connection with our sense experience. Such lines of inquiry connected me to the roots of Eastern philosophy and the corresponding partial manifestations in the Western counterparts. This ultimately led me to realize the significance of self-inquiry (
atmavichaar
). Now, I continue to work aimlessly on various paths of inquiry where the ``I'' directs me. This often gives me the realization of the undecidability of a `foundation'.
During my journey as a researcher, I have had invaluable experience and honor of getting the opportunity to interact and `teach' (discuss with) young and inquisitive minds in ISI Kolkata and Christ University Bangalore, before I joined NIT Jamshedpur in October, 2024.
NOTE - In this current homepage, only my works after 2020 are listed. In case one is interested to find my full publication list, I recommend visiting my Google Scholar page.

Dr Akhileshwar Kumar Singh
Associate Professor
Civil Engineering
·
Dr. AKhileshwar Kumar Singh
is Associate Professor in Civil Engineering at National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur. He
        graduated in 1988 (1984 - 1988) with a first-class with distinction in Civil
        Engineering from NIT, Jamshedpur (Formerly RIT Jamshedpur, Ranchi University,
        Ranchi). He has M. Tech. in Geotechnical
        Engineering (civil Engineering) from GEC Jabalpur (MP) in 1993 and secured
1
ST
Rank in the RDV Jabalpur. He completed his Ph. D. in Civil
        Engineering (Geotechnical Engineering) in 2004 from IIT Roorkee under QIP scheme.
He has completed approx.
29 years
of
            teaching in Civil Engineering, research and consultancy experience in the field of Geotechnical
            Engineering. His primary area of research includes Seepage and their
            applications in water retaining earthen structures and its foundation, Stability of Structure, Foundation
            Engineering, Ground Improvement, Soil-structure Interaction, Rock Mechanics, River Bank
            Filtration, Tailing Dam, Waste Pond [Analytical, Numerical & Experimental]. He has good
exposure of waste pond and landfill related issues while attending the International Conference,
ICEST – 2014 (June) American Academy of Science, Houston, Texas
(USA).
He has supervised two Ph. D. thesis and other two are in under progress. He is Principal Investigator
of sponsored project of Rs. 10 Lakh sanctioned by NHAI Ranchi [NH- 33 & NH - 06].
He has authored more than 80
        research papers and technical articles including 20 referred Journal
        Publications [ASCE, Taylor & Francis, Springer].
Dr. Singh has authored one book and Co-authored five book chapters.
He is also a reviewer of several International
        Journals in the areas of Geotechnical Engineering. He has setup a new
        laboratory named “Rock Mechanics Laboratory”.
He was member of STA PMGSY Jharkhand. He is also member of
            State Committee on Dam Safety, Jharkhand.
As
            a Consulting Geotechnical Engineer, he has successfully executed different
            problems and their solutions to the challenging field problems faced by different
            organizations nearby Jamshedpur and Jharkhand. In addition, he has been
            contributed significantly to the Institute’s corporate life and successfully completed
            important administrative responsibilities such as two and half years tenure as
            Head, Department of Civil Engineering, NIT, Jamshedpur (2008 – 2009 & 2020
            - 2022), Warden, P/I Construction and Maintenance, Associate Dean (A & IR, P & D). He has been
instrumental in starting M. Tech. [GATE] in
            Geotechnical Engineering in 2013-14 in the Department of Civil Engineering, NIT, Jamshedpur.
He is life member of Indian Geotechnical Society [IGS], Indian
            Society for Rock Mechanics and Tunnelling Technology [ISRMTT] and Aff. M. ASCE.

Dr Amit Kumar
Assistant Professor
Electronics and Communication Engineering
Dr. Amit Kumar currently working as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering, NIT (Jamshedpur). He also served as a contractual faculty in NIT, Jalandhar(Punjab) during 10-Fab-2022 to 31-May-2022. He did his B.Tech from Galgotias College of Engineering and Technology, Gr. Noida in Electronics and Communication Engineering in 2011. He completed his M.Tech from National Institute of Technology, Durgapur (W.B.), with a specialization in Microelectronics and VLSI in 2014. He received his Ph.D. degree from Indian Institute of Technology (BHU), Varanasi (U.P.), with a specialization in Microelectronics in 2021. He received Visvesvaraya Fellowship funded by MeitY Govt. of India for pursuing his PhD. His research area primarily focused on fabrication and characterization of various Thin Film Devices such as Photovoltaic Devices, Photo Detectors, Thin Film Transistors (TFTs), and Gas Sensors etc. Synthesis of several Nano-Structured (Quantum Dots, Nano rods, Nano wires etc.) metal oxide such as ZnO, TiO
2
, and MoO
3
etc. is also a part of his research area.

Dr Arjun Kumar
Assistant Professor
Electronics and Communication Engineering
I received my B.Tech. degree in electronics and communication engineering from (National Institute of Science & Technology) Biju Patnaik University
of Technology, Odisha, India, in 2013 and the
Ph.D. degree from IIT (Banaras Hindu University),

My current research interests include computational electromagnetics, slow-wave structure, high
power microwave sources, metamaterial based HPM
source, plasma filled HPM source, and metamaterial based applications.

Dr Arnab Kumar Sinha
Assistant Professor
Civil Engineering
Dr. Arnab Kumar Sinha
is presently serving as Assistant professor in the Department of Civil Engineering.
Dr. Sinha holds a PhD in Structural Engineering
    from IIT Guwahati (2023), M.Tech in Structural Engineering from NIT Silchar
    (2015), and a B.E. in Civil Engineering from Assam Engineering College, Guwahati
    (2012). His Research Area includes development, characterization of novel
    retrofitting material and its application in rehabilitation of RCC structures. During his PhD, he
    contributed significantly to the field of Retrofitting and Rehabilitation and published several research papers in
    prestigious SCI and SCOPUS-indexed journals and also presented papers at
    renowned international conferences. In addition to his academic achievements, he has
    a rich blend of industrial and teaching experience. After his BE, he joined Patel Engineering Ltd. and worked on a hydropower project of 10MW in Tenga valley, Arunachal Pradesh. After his M.Tech he joined NHIDCL and gained hands-on
    expertise in handling large scale building and road Projects of Assam under MORTH.
    As an educator, he has served as an Assistant Professor in the Department of
    Civil Engineering at NIT Silchar, GCU Guwahati and in State Govt. college of
    Assam, BVEC for more than 3 years, imparting knowledge to the next generation
    of engineers. Dr. Sinha also worked as a Teaching Assistant at IIT Guwahati for
    six years, contributing to the academic community and enhancing learning
    experiences. Furthermore, he also served in the National Program on Technology
    Enhanced Learning (NPTEL) under the Ministry of Education, Government of India,
    furthering the reach of quality education in civil engineering.

Dr Ashok Kumar Barik
Assistant Professor
Mechanical Engineering
I completed my B.E in Mechanical Engineering from Berhampur University in the year 2001. I completed M. Tech degree in Thermal Engineering from Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur in the Year 2007, and then the doctoral degree from Mechanical Engineering at Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur in the Year 2015. My doctoral thesis is based on the air entertainment into an Infrared Suppression Device. Later, I worked in various frontier areas of research like, nanofluids and nano-enhanced ionic liquids (NEILs), solar energy storage, two-phase flows (in particular, the gas-solid flows and air-water flows), heat transfer enhancement, natural and forced convection inclusive of  turbulent flow fields to name a few. In the recent past, I and my co-researchers started working on the bio-inspired flows, in particular, the study on the aero-fluid dynamics of dragonflies, small insects as well as fishes. I and our research team have some research experience on handling the sponsored projects (SERB, Govt. of India and DST, Govt. of Odisha). The former project has been completed successfully in the Year 2022; whereas the later one is still active, and we expect to complete it soon. I also act as a regular reviewer for Scientific articles of repute for various publishing houses like, Elsevier, Springer, Willy, Taylor and Francis, American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME), American Institute of Physics (AIP), American Institute of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA), etc. We welcome enthusiastic students and researchers from various Departments of the same Institute as well as other Institutes (both from India and abroad) to work with us in multidisciplinary grey areas.

Dr Ashwinee Kumar
Assistant Professor
Metallurgical and Materials Engineering
Dr. Ashwinee Kumar is currently an Assistant Professor in the Department of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering at NIT Jamshedpur. Prior to this, he served as an Adhoc Faculty and Visiting Assistant Professor in the same department at NIT Warangal.
He completed his PhD at Trinity College Dublin on an Irish Research Council Scholarship and holds an Integrated Dual Degree (B.Tech and M.Tech) in Metallurgical Engineering from IIT (BHU). His research primarily focuses on computational materials science (MD, DFT), as well as physical and mechanical metallurgy.
Outside of his academic pursuits, he enjoys poetry, playing the North Indian classical bamboo flute, cycling, cricket and exploring philosophy.

Dr. Balram Ambade is an Associate Professor and former Head of Department at the Department of Chemistry, National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur, India. He has been in academia for over 20 years and has immensely contributed to original research in atmospheric and water chemistry and environmental remediation of toxic metals, microplastics, and PFAS. He is the recipient of several prestigious awards, including the Early Career Research (ECR) award by the Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB), the Marie Curie Award from Hyytiälä Forest Field Station, Helsinki, Finland, the Groningen Biomolecular Sciences and Biotechnology Institute (GBB) award from the University of Groningen, Netherland, and the Young Scientist Award from China in 2014, and the NASA Earth Science Division Modeling, MAP award by Météo-France in Toulouse, France. He is currently a Guest Editor for Special Issues of "Science of the Total Environment" (Elsevier, IF: 9.8), "Physics and Chemistry of the Earth" (Elsevier, IF: 3.8), "Environmental Science and Pollution Research" (Springer, IF: 5.8), and "Sustainability" (MDPI, IF: 3.8). He has published over 100 Science Citation Indexed journal articles and ten book chapters. He has authored seven books with Elsevier, Springer, Taylor and Francis, Nova Science, LP Germany, and Scholars Press. He has supervised 10 Ph.D. , 11 M.Tech., and 48 M.Sc. students. Currently, he is mentoring and supervising six Ph.D. students.

Dr Basanta Bhowmik
Assistant Professor
Electronics and Communication Engineering
Dr. B Bhowmik currently working as assistant professor in the Dept. of Electronics and Communication Engineering, National Institute of Technology, Jamshedpur. His post graduation from Indian Institute of Information Technology, Gwalior with specialization VLSI Design. He was PhD fellow at Indian Institute of Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur, India. His research interest includes Semiconducting material and devices for sensing, and Photovoltaics. He is the author and co-author of fifty two research article of international repute. He received CSIR SRF fellowship award for pursuing his PhD. He received the best poster award in the event Research Scholar Colloquium organized by IIEST Shibpur in 2014. He was awarded second best PhD thesis by Instutte of Smart Structure and System, IISc Bangalore. He is the member of IEEE, IEEE Electron Device Society, IEEE Sensor Council, IEEE Nanotechnology Council and life member of Institute of Smart Structure and System, India. He presently served as an active reviewer of many journals including IEEE Sensor Journal (IEEE), RSC Advances (RSC), ACS Sensor (ACS), Smart Materials and Structures (IOP), Journal of Physics Chemistry of Solids (Elsevier), Journal of Nanoparticle Research (Springer), BioNanoscience (Springer), Microelectronics Journal (Elsevier), Vaccum (Elsevier) etc.

Dr Bhupali Dutta
Assistant Professor
Civil Engineering
Dr. Bhupali Dutta is presently serving as an Assistant Professor in the Civil Engineering Department, at NIT Jamshedpur.
She completed her B. E. (Bachelor of Engineering) degree in
Civil Engineering from Assam Engineering College in the year 2011.
After
completing her bachelor’s, she joined Simplex Infrastructures Limited as an
Assistant Engineer for their Greenfield airport project in Durgapur, West
Bengal. She then joined BITS Pilani, Pilani for her M. E. (Master of
Engineering) degree in Civil Engineering, with a specialization in Transportation
Engineering in 2012. In 2014, she joined IIT Kanpur to pursue her Ph.D. in
Civil Engineering with a specialization in Transportation Engineering. She
received her Ph.D. degree in 2021. Her Ph.D. work is related to
understanding driver behavior in weak lane-disciplined traffic using
naturalistic driving data. Her research interests are the analysis of road user
behavior in different traffic conditions, road safety, pavement maintenance,
and the use of sustainable materials in civil engineering.

Dr Binay  Kumar
Assistant Professor
Metallurgical and Materials Engineering
Dr. Binay Kumar is currently working
as an Assistant professor in the Department of Metallurgical and Materials
Engineering, National Institute of Technology (NIT) Jamshedpur, Jharkhand,
India since Nov. 2022. He completed his M.Tech. and Ph.D. from the
Department of Metallurgical and Materials Engineering, Indian Institute
of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur, in the years 2015 and 2021,
respectively.
Before joining NIT Jamshedpur, he
was working in Research and Development Division of ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel
(AMNS) India, Surat, Gujarat.
He has also worked
in the Foundry Division of Tata Motors Ltd., Jamshedpur before enrolling at IIT
Kharagpur for his M.Tech. course.
His major area of research interest
includes alternative routes of ironmaking and steelmaking, process optimization,
exergy analysis, energy and emission control,
and thermodynamic
modelling. Apart from this, he is also well-versed with the application of thermodynamic
software like Thermo-Calc and FactSage in his research field
. He is a life member of the Indian Institute of Metals, Kolkata, India and a member of the Institute of Indian Foundrymen.

Dr Deepak Kumar
Assistant Professor
Mechanical Engineering
Biography
Deepak is working in the field of damage mechanics of composite Materials, Nanocomposites, Smart Materials, Product design and development of biomaterials. He received a bachelor’s degree
in mechanical engineering from MAHE, India; Master’s degree in Computer Aided Analysis and Design from BITS, Mesra, India and PhD in Aerospace Engineering from Gyeongsa
ng National University, South Korea. His PhD thesis was about multi-scale damage model for composite structures, which considered the onset and evolution of intra-laminar matrix cracking and interlaminar delamination in various ply-configurations considering the mixed-mode failure. Deepak also gained valuable experimental expertise in the areas of automated fibre placement technologies and composite bolted-joint mechanics.  His latest research interests are the development of nanocomposites for development of supercapacitors and energy devices, data-driven material design, metamaterials, and artificial tissues. Kumar is the principal investigator of an ongoing research project. project funded by the DST (India and Serbia) of the Government of India. Recently, he has received another project from the MSME Innovation Scheme, GOI. He is currently supervising Six doctoral students and has supervised nine master's theses. He is also a reviewer of various reputed international journals.

Prof Goutam Sutradhar
Professor
Mechanical Engineering
Prof. (Dr.) Goutam Sutradhar
currently the
Director at the National Institute of Technology
Jamshedpur,
since 12th May 2023. Before this, he served as the Director of NIT Manipur for a full term of
five years. He completed his Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering from Jalpaiguri Government
Engineering College, West Bengal in 1984. He subsequently earned his Master's degree in Mechanical
Engineering with a specialization in Foundry Technology from IIT Kharagpur in 1986. He completed his
Ph.D. in Engineering from Birla Institute of Technology (BIT) Mesra, Ranchi. After working for five years
in Hindustan Motors Limited and Indian Railways, he joined as a faculty member at the National Institute
of Foundry & Forge Technology, Ranchi, Jharkhand in 1991. He later served at Serampore Textile
College, West Bengal and Kalyani Government Engineering College, West Bengal for about ten years
before joining Jadavpur University, Kolkata, as a Professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering
in 2005. He has supervised more than 20 M.Tech thesis and 21 Ph.D. students in the field of Metal Matrix
Composites, Polymer Matrix Composites, Development of Environment-friendly Materials, Synthesis of
Forged Powder Metallurgy Components, and Metal Casting Processes. He has supervised many research
projects sponsored by AICTE, New Delhi; CSIR, New Delhi; UGC, New Delhi; DST, New Delhi. He has
authored two books, namely "Design and Manufacturing: An Integrated Approach" published by Oxford &
IBH, and "Foundry Process Design" published by New Age Publishers, New Delhi. He has
published over 125 technical papers in referred journals of national and international importance and
presented more than 50 technical papers at national and international conferences.

Prof Hira Lal Yadav
Professor
Department of Physics
Prof. Hira Lal Yadav
is a distinguished academic and researcher in Experimental Physics, specialized
in laser-based instrumentation, holography, and photonics. He obtained his
M.Sc. degree in Physics from the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi in
1986 and Ph.D. in in instrumentation from IDDC, IIT Delhi in
1992. His doctoral work focused on holographic lenses in speckle metrology and
solar concentration. He further pursued his research work as a Post-Doctroral
Fellow of CSIR, New Delhi from 1993-1996.
 
He has been serving
as a faculty member in the Department of Physics at NIT
Jamshedpur since 1996. During this period, he also served as
Assistant Professor at Netaji Subhas Institute of Technology (NSIT), Delhi, for
6 months in the year 2000 on lien from NIT Jamshedpur. With over three
decades of teaching and research experience, Prof. Yadav has contributed
significantly to the fields of optical metrology, holographic solar
concentrators, and photonic instrumentation. He has established the Photonics
Laboratory at NIT Jamshedpur and has guided several Ph.D. scholars and
postgraduate dissertations. His research contribution is reflected in reputed
SCI/ Scopus-indexed journals, proceedings of international conferences
including  IPR patents/design and several
sponsored research projects funded by AICTE and MHRD.
Prof. Yadav has also held various
academic and administrative positions, including Head of the Department of
Physics, Associate Dean (Faculty Welfare), Deputy Registrar (Establishment),
Professor-in-Charge of the Finishing School and Chief Vigilance Officer at NIT
Jamshedpur. He continues to actively pursue research in holography, optical
metrology, and renewable energy applications, while mentoring the next
generation of physicists and engineers.

Dr.J.Jayapal is
presently working as an Assistant Professor at National Institute of
Technology, Jamshedpur, Jharkand. He earned his BE Degree in Civil Engineering
from PSG College of Technology, Coimbatore affiliated to Anna University in the
year 2007. He then worked as an Engineer Trainee at DLF Consultants New Delhi
for about one year and was involved in the construction of an IT Park in
Manapakkam, Chennai. He then obtained his ME degree specialized in Soil
Mechanics and Foundation Engineering from the College of Engineering Guindy
Campus (CEG) -Anna University in the year 2010. Following this, he
had worked as an Assistant Professor for few years in private engineering
colleges teaching different subjects in civil engineering. He then earned his
PhD Degree in Civil Engineering with a specialization in Geotechnical
Engineering from Indian Institute of Technology, Madras (IIT-M) in
the year 2021. Afterwards, he joined as an Institute Post-Doctoral Fellow at
Indian Institute of Technology -Bombay, Mumbai (IIT-B) before joining the
current position.
Dr Jayapal has
participated in several national and international geotechnical engineering
conferences during his research tenure. He has won two Best Presenter
Awards for his conference papers presented at IGC-2019
GeoIndus organized by IGS Surat Chapter, NIT Surat, Gujarat and at
IGC 2024 (GEST) organized by IGS Aurangabad Chapter, MIT -
Aurangabad, Maharashtra & Springer Nature award worth (EUR-75).
His research interests
include, Soft Ground Improvement, Geosynthetic Encased Granular Columns,
Numerical Modelling using PLAXIS, MATLAB Programming, Pavement Geotechniques,
Geo-Naturals for problems associated in Rural Areas and on the Innovative
Materials in Civil Engineering.

Interested PhD aspirants, PG scholars who are willing to conduct research in
any of these areas can drop an email expressing their interest.

Dr Kamal Pal
Associate Professor
Production and Industrial Engineering
Dr.
        Kamal Pal
is currently working as an Associate Professor in the department of
        Production and Industrial Engineering, National Institute of Technology (NIT)
        Jamshedpur, Jharkhand, India since 5th March 2024. He received his B.Engg.in
        Production Engineering from Jadavpur University in 2001, M.Engg. from Bengal
        Engineering College (Deemed University), Shibpur presently Indian Institute of
        Engineering Science and Technology, Shibpur in 2003 and Ph.D. from Indian
        Institute of Technology Kharagpur in Mechanical Engineering in 2010.
Prior
        to Joining NIT Jamshedpur Dr. Pal has served as an Associate Professor (2016-2024) and Assistant Professor/ Reader (2013-2016) in the
        Department of Production Engineering at Veer Surendra Sai University of
        Technology, Burla, Govt. of Odisha, India. He also worked as an
        Associate Professor (2011-2013), Assistant Professor (2010-2011) and Lecturer (2003-2010) in the School of Mechanical Engineering at KIIT University,
        Bhubaneswar.
His
        research interests include optimization and real-time monitoring of joining
        processes, wire arc additive manufacturing, machining and non-conventional machining processes. He has
        supervised more than twenty MTech thesis and five Ph.D. students in the field of process monitoring in friction stir welding of
        thermoplastics, gas metal arc welding of dissimilar materials, machining of
        hard steels and fibre-reinforced composites. He has published more than 35 research
        papers in reputed journals (SCI/Scopus) and more than 40 conference proceedings of national
        and international repute. He serves as a reviewer for various international
        journals. He is a  member of Indian Institute of Welding (IIW-INDIA).
Beyond
        his academic interests, Dr. Pal has actively engaged in administrative
        responsibilities, including Head of the department in Production Engineering (2019-2022), Metallurgical & Materials Engineering (2018-19) and Institute nodal officer, Scholarship (2022-2024) at VSSUT Burla.

Dr Kethavath Raghavendra Naik
Assistant Professor
Electrical Engineering
K. Raghavendra Naik is currently serving as assistant professor in the Electrical engineering department NIT Jamshedpur, India. He completed his B. Tech from VIgnan's university, Guntur. M.Tech and Ph.D from Visvesvaraya National Institute of Technology Nagpur, India.
Personnel Interest:
My strong motivation as a researcher is we should be useful
        to the society in the best possible way we can. I am an optimistic researcher in Electric vehicle domain. What excites me about electric
        vehicles is the challenges it offers as far as control aspect, energy management aspect, voltage stability aspect, Vehicle-grid and Grid-Vehicle aspects are concerned. Eventually, the large
        adoption of EVs across the globe has positive and negative impacts
        on the utility grid. The positive impact of EVs on grid is its coordinated participation in the grids peak and off peak load demand. The negative
        impact is EVs fleet charging during peak load demand may cause a threat to resiliency and reliability of the utility grid. Therefore, to maintain the reliability and resiliency of main grid against the intermittency of EV customer an intelligent energy management strategy is obligatory.  I am open to collaboration in the following object oriented research works.
1. Artificial Intelligence based Energy Management strategy for EV charging station integrated DC Microgrid
2. Designing Transformer less EV fast charger topologies.
3. Intelligent Power Management of DC Microgrid under highly stochastic load conditions
4. Intelligent control algorithms for Voltage control  of Isolated DC Microgrids
Please find my potential publication  @ https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=YjIK-p8AAAAJ&hl=en

        Engineering, Member of the Departmental Purchase Committee, Faculty charge of
        the institute’s annual magazine ‘MANTHAN’, Warden of Girls Hostel, Served as

Dr Kundan Kumar
Assistant Professor
Electrical Engineering
Dr.
        Kundan Kumar (M’ 2013, SM’ 2021 IEEE USA)
has
completed his B. Tech. from the IET MJP
    Rohilkhand University, Bareilly, in 2008. He has received the M. Tech. degree
    from NIT Jamshedpur, Jamshedpur, India, and the Ph.D. degree from the
    University of Padova, Padova, Italy, both in Electrical Engineering, in 2010
    and 2016, respectively. Prior to NIT Manipur, he has worked as an Assistant
    Professor with the School of Electrical Engineering, Kalinga Institute of
    Industrial Technology, deemed to be a university, in Bhubaneswar, India. Dr.
    Kumar received the Silver Medal for securing the first position during his M.
    Tech. course. He has also been awarded a University Fellowship for a Ph. D.
    course at the University of Padova, Italy. He has also been awarded the Best
    Presentation Recognition award at IECON, held in Japan in 2015, and the Best
    Paper award in IEEE STPEC-2021 at Bilaspur, India. He has chaired and
    co-chaired the various Technical Sessions in the prestigious IEEE International
    Conferences, such as IECON, PEDES, ICPEE, GUCON, and SEFET. He has published
    more than 50 research articles in reputed International Journals and Conference
    Proceedings, 7 book chapters, and 5 Indian patents. He has supervised 02 Ph.D. scholars, and 04 are under spervision. He has published one edited
    book entitled “Electric Vehicle Propulsion Drives and Charging Systems,” in
    Taylor and Francis, CRC Press. Presently, he is editing a book entitled “Recent
    Advances and Emerging Technologies in Multi-Level Inverters,” which will be
    published in River Publishers. He has organized the IEEE International
    Conference on Power Electronics and Energy (ICPEE-2021) and International
    Conference on Science, Technology, and Engineering (ICSTE-2023) with the
    capacity of organizing secretary, as well as the 2nd IEEE International
    Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments and Applications
    (ICIDeA-2023) with the capacity of Conference Chair. He has also organized the “2024 IEEE 1st International Conference on Green Industrial
    Electronics and Sustainable Technologies (GIEST-2024)” which was held at
    NIT Manipur from 25–26 Oct. 2024 with the capacity of Conference Chair. He is a senior member of the IEEE (USA) and a
    Life member of the Institution of Engineers (IE), India. He is the reviewer of
    IEEE journals and transactions such as TIE, TPEL, JESTPE, and various reputed
    conferences such as IECON, PEDES, INDICON, and PEMC. His research interests
    include Electric Vehicles and their charging infrastructures, Wireless Power
    Transfer Systems, Dynamic Wireless Charging Systems, Propulsion Drive Systems
    for EVs, Application of Wide Bandgap Semiconductor Devices (i.e. GaN &
    SiC), High-Efficiency Power Converters, Soft Switching, Multi-port Converters,
    Single-Active Bridge (SAB), Dual Active Bridge (DAB) Converters, and Offshore
    Wind Energy System.

Dr Kuntal Maji
Assistant Professor
Production and Industrial Engineering
Dr. Kuntal Maji is
        currently working as an Assistant Professor in the Department of
        Production and Industrial Engineering, National Institute of Technology (NIT)
        Jamshedpur, Jharkhand, India since September 2022.
He completed his B.E.
        (Hons.) in Production Engineering from Jadavpur University in 2005. He had
        worked in industry as Graduate Engineer Trainee and Executive Engineer in the
        L.J. Machinery & Co. Ltd., Kyd Street, Kolkata (2005-2006) in
        Production Division
. He has done
M.Tech.
        in Manufacturing Science and Engineering from the Department of Mechanical
        Engineering, Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur in 2009. He
        has done his PhD in the area of laser materials processing during 2009-2014
        from the Mechanical Engineering Department of IIT Kharagpur.  Before
        joining NIT Jamshedpur, he has served as Assistant Professor in Mechanical
        Engineering Department of MNIT Jaipur (2015) and NIT Patna (2015-2022).
Dr.
        Maji teaches subjects like metal forming, additive manufacturing, CAD/CAM,
        manufacturing processes, Machine learning, CAD/CAM Laboratory, Workshop
        Practices, Robotics laboratory, Advanced Manufacturing laboratory etc. He has
        developed metal forming and additive manufacturing laboratory in the PIE
        Department, and upgradation of the facilities like CNC Vertical Machining
        centre, auto cast software etc. in the CAD/CAM laboratory. Presently he is
        supervising 3 PhD scholars and UG/PG students. He has introduced subjects like
        Additive Manufacturing, machine learning etc., and he has contributed in
        developing M. Tech. program on “Smart Manufacturing” in the PIE Department.
His
        major area of research interest includes metal forming, metal additive
        manufacturing, process modelling and optimization of manufacturing
        processes focusing on process-structure-property-performance analysis towards
        improvement and development of manufacturing methods and products employing
        numerical simulations like finite element analysis and machine learning
        techniques. Dr. Maji has completed one SERB sponsored project funded by Govt.
        of India as the Principal Investigator (2017-2020). He has two ongoing
        sponsored projects 2024-2025. He has been involved in consultancy work on
        casting simulation, and industrial collaborations on welding process
        simulations using finite element method. He has guided four Ph.D. theses and
        ten Master's theses. He has published thirty papers in various
        international journals, twenty five papers in conference proceedings or other
        journals, patents, and four book chapters.

Prof Mani Kant Paswan
Professor
Mechanical Engineering
Dr. Manikant Paswan
(Professor in Deptt. Of Mechanical
            Engg., Dean Faculty Welfare)
NIT Jamshedpur
Prof. Mani Kant Paswan has been a Professor in the Department of Mechanical Engi
neering
since May 2004 and has served as Dean (Faculty Welfare) since August 2021. Prior to joining
as Dean (F/W), he was Head of the Mechanical Engineering Department at National Institute
of Technology (NIT) Jamshedpur, India, for 2.5 years (2018-2021). He is serving as President
Nominee at all NIT faculty recruitments since 2023, as well as at Central University Guru
Ghasidas Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh, in faculty recruitments since September 2022. He also served
as Senate member of NIT Meghalaya from 2019-2022. He is working as academic council and
Board of Studies member of various universities such as Sarla-Birla University Ranchi, Amity
University Kolkata, Amity University Ranchi, Arka-Jain University Jamshedpur etc. He is
working as Nominated Moderator by AICTE of 2 Universities in Jharkhand Ram Govind Singh
Engineering College Koderma and Chandravanshi Engineering College Gadhwa. He is
working as an Accessor in NAAC and NBA since 3 years and 4 years respectively.
During his nearly three-decade teaching and research career, he has been an investigator on
several funded research projects in MHRD (R&D), TEQIP, and various consultancy work.
Renewable energy, composite materials, power plant engineering, and industrial applications
are among his current research interests. He has over a hundred papers published in prestigious
journals and has attended over 25 conferences. He was supervisor and research supervisor
associate of eight PhDs to date, with another six currently in progress. He has also supervised
63+ M.Tech scholars and 31+ B.Tech project groups to date. Prof. Paswan is a leading
proponent of solar thermal heating systems and natural fibre composite materials.

Dr Manthirikul Sandeep
Assistant Professor
Civil Engineering
Dr. Manthirikul Sandeep is an Assistant Professor at the Department of Civil Engineering, National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur. Before joining NIT Jamshedpur he worked as a Post Doctorate Research Fellow at IIT Bombay and IIT Jammu. He did his Masters from University College of Engineering, Osmania University, India in 2018 and Ph.D. from Visvesvaraya National Institute of Technology, Nagpur, India in 2023. His research interests are Transportation simulation & modelling, Pedestrian Safety and Road user behaviour. His Ph.D. dissertation work was carried on guidelines for the Grade separated pedestrian crossing facilities. He proposed new crossing warrants for the installation of Grade Separated Pedestrian Crossing Facilities in India. The outcome of his research may fill the gaps in one of the Indian Road Congress codes i.e., IRC:103:2022. Dr. Sandeep is a certified Road Safety Auditor and has completed certification courses in Road Safety from VNIT, Nagpur in 2021. He was the moderator of several 15-Days Road Safety Auditor Certification Courses conducted at VNIT Nagpur in association with the Indian Roads Congress and the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways (Govt. of India) for the training of working professionals in the field of road safety. He is a member of various professional bodies like Indian Roads Congress (IRC) and American Society of Civil Engineers. Dr. Sandeep was involved in several road safety audit works (Design stage and existing stage) of national highways in the Jammu region.

Dr Mayuri Baruah
Assistant Professor
Production and Industrial Engineering
Dr. Mayuri Baruah is currently working as an Assistant Professor at the Department of Production and Industrial Engineering, National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur, Jharkhand since 2018. She obtained her B.E. (Mechanical Engineering) from Dibrugarh University, Assam, and her Integrated Ph.D. from the Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati, Assam in the year 2017. Her Ph.D. thesis title was Experimental investigation and numerical modeling of Plasma and Laser micro welding processes. Later she worked as Assistant Professor (on contract), Mechanical Engineering Department, Assam Engineering College, Assam, from 5th January 2018 to 4th June 2018. She also worked as a Temporary faculty at NIT Raipur from August to December 2018. She also worked as a Virtual faculty for gate coaching in Mechanical Engineering at Ufaber Edutech Pvt. Ltd, Mumbai. Her major areas of research interests include Welding, Additive Manufacturing, Numerical Modeling, Python, Artificial Intelligence, Characterization, and Optimization of manufacturing processes. She has published 11 papers in international journals and 10 Conferences. She is currently editing a Book “Next Generation Materials and Technologies” published in Select Proceedings in Materials by Springer. She has also published 2 book chapters. Till now, 5 research scholars are working under her guidance. 6 M.Tech. projects and more than 20 B.Tech. (Hons.) projects have been completed so far.

Dr Munendra Singh
Assistant Professor
Electronics and Communication Engineering
Dr. Munendra
Singh is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Electronics and
Communication Engineering at National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur. Prior
to his current role, Dr. Singh received his post-doctoral research training from the MR Research division at Johns Hopkins University, USA from June 2021 to October
2024. He worked as an Assistant Professor at Manipal Institute of Technology in
Manipal where he engaged in teaching and research in the deep learning and image
processing domain for two and half years. Dr. Singh specializes in developing
reliable physics-informed deep learning-based solutions for the reconstruction
and quantification of MRI data, making significant contributions in quantifying
multiple tissue parameters from a single scan of the human brain and reducing
the overall scan time. He defended his PhD (Optimization techniques-based
algorithms for de-noising, enhancement and segmentation of MRI data) in 2019
from the Indian Institute of Technology (Banaras Hindu University), Varanasi.
He earned his master's degree in Instrumentation from the National Institute of
Technology, Kurukshetra, in 2012 and his bachelor's degree in Electronics and
Communication from the University Institute of Engineering and Technology, CSJM
University, Kanpur, in 2010.

Dr Naveen Kumar Veldurthi
Assistant Professor
Department of Chemistry
‘Heterogeneous catalysis’ is my primary research interest with which I have been in association for the past twelve years. I completed my Ph.D. from Osmania University, Hyderabad in 2016 and my doctoral thesis is on investigating several strategies to develop visible light active semiconductor photocatalysts for Environmental remediation. After that, with my profound interest in ‘Water splitting’, I joined the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bangalore as a National post-doctoral fellow (NPDF) and developed several novel composite photocatalyst systems for hydrogen fuel generation until I joined NIT Jamshedpur as Assistant Professor in 2018.
My long-term research agenda is to address the worsening global climate change issue by contributing to clean energy research i.e., clean hydrogen fuel production and CO
2
reduction into chemical fuels.
Please check out our website @
https://www.ceemlab.in
to learn more about the exciting work we're doing at the Clean Energy & Environmental Materials (CEEM) Laboratory.

Dr Neha  Agnihotri
Assistant Professor
Department of Physics
Dr. Neha Agnihotri holds a Ph.D. in Physics from Banaras Hindu University (BHU), India, and completed her postdoctoral research at the University of Saskatchewan, Canada. She currently serves as an Assistant Professor of Physics at the National Institute of Technology, Jamshedpur. Prior to her appointment at NIT Jamshedpur, she was  an INSPIRE Faculty at the Indian Institute of Technology (BHU), Varanasi.
Dr. Agnihotri's research interests encompass graphene and other two-dimensional materials, quantum materials, and their applications in nanoelectronic devices, solar cells, and sensor technologies. She has authored several publications in esteemed international journals and has received notable recognitions, including the DST-INSPIRE Faculty Award and the SERB-Start-up Research Grant. Additionally, she contributes as a reviewer for several international journals, reflecting her commitment to advancing the field of physics.

Dr Neha Jaiswal
Assistant Professor
Department of Humanities, Social Sciences and Management
Dr. Neha Jaiswal has done her Ph.D. at the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur. She has also worked as a Postdoctoral Research Associate at IIM Ahmedabad. Her doctoral thesis is titled “Mergers, Acquisitions and Competition Law: A study of Selected Industries from the Indian Manufacturing Sector.” During her Post-Doc at IIM Ahmedabad, she tried to explore the impact of mergers and acquisitions on the innovative capabilities of Indian pharmaceutical firms. She also worked as a researcher at the Combination Division of the Competition Commission of India, New Delhi. She has published research articles in peer-reviewed international journals and presented her research at various national and international conferences and workshops.   Her research interests include Mergers & Acquisitions (Economics of Strategy), Innovation, and Competition Law & policy.

Dr Omhari Gupta
Assistant Professor
Electrical Engineering
Dr. Gupta earned his PhD in Electrical Engineering from the IIT Roorkee, India, in 2017. He was awarded the prestigious Canadian Queen Elizabeth II Diamond Jubilee Scholarship, enabling him to conduct research at Ontario Tech University, Canada, as a visiting researcher in 2017.
Since 2018
, Dr. Gupta has been an
Assistant Professor in the Department of Electrical Engineering
at
NIT Jamshedpur
, India. Dr. Gupta
co-founded
the "Electric Power and Renewable Energy Conference (
EPREC
)" series and has authored/edited seven books. His academic contributions include
about 98 publications, with 35 journal papers and one granted patent
. He serves on the Springer Nature Journal
Scientific Reports
editorial board
and is a
Senior Member of IEEE
. Additionally, he is a reviewer for numerous reputed journals, including IEEE Transactions on Power Delivery, Electric Power Systems Research, etc. His research interests encompass power system protection, microgrids, renewable energy-based distributed generation, and electric power quality.

Dr Pranab Kumar Kundu
Associate Professor
Mechanical Engineering
Dr. Pranab Kumar Kundu is a researcher and educator specializing in microfluidics, heat spreaders, and biomedical applications. He earned his Ph.D. in Microfabrications & Microfluidics from the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur in 2015. His work focuses on improving microscale heat spreaders for electronic components and developing microfluidic-based point-of-care diagnostic devices. Dr. Kundu also has experiences in processing DTM super alloys like Ti-6Al-4V and Nimonic through grinding and EDM.
Dr. Kundu completed his B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering from Kalyani Government Engineering College (KGEC) in 1999 and his Master's in Mechanical Engineering from Jadavpur University in 2002. Over his career, he has served as a Lecturer at various institutes, Junior and Senior Project Officers, and a Research Associate at IIT Kharagpur. He has also worked as an Assistant Professor at National Institute of Technology Sikkim and Motilal Nehru National Institute of Technology Allahabad prior to joining as an Associate Professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering, National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur.
In addition to his academic work, Dr. Kundu has taken on several administrative roles, including chairing sports committees and coordinating cultural activities. He has received honors such as prestigious VISVESVARAYA YOUNG FACULTY RESEARCH FELLOWSHIP and Best Paper Awards at international conferences. His research contributions include numerous publications and notable text books on Engineering Mechanics, Thermodynamics, and Thermal Engineering.
