Dr Raj Nandkeolyar
Associate Professor
Department Of Mathematics
Dr. Raj Nandkeolyar
Ph. D. (IIT ISM Dhanbad, 2011), M. Phil. (IIT ISM Dhanbad, 2007)
Post-Doctoral Fellowship (University of KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa)
Biography:.
Dr. Raj Nandkeolyar is currently Associate Professor and Head of the Department of Mathematics, National Institute of Technology, Jamshedpur, India. He joined NIT Jamshedpur as an Assistant Professor (Grade-I) on June 08, 2018. Before joining NIT Jamshedpur, he spent 4 years (July 2014 - June 2018) as an Assistant Professor in the School of Mathematics, Thapar University, Patiala, India, One and a half years (January 2013 - July 2014) as a Post-Doctoral Fellow at the School of Mathematics, Statistics & Computer Science, University of KwaZulu-Natal, Pietermaritzburg, South Africa, and 2 years (February 2011 - January 2013) as an Assistant Professor of Mathematics at the School of Applied Sciences, KIIT University, Bhubaneswar, India. He has about 14 years of teaching/research experience. Dr. Nandkeolyar obtained his M. Phil. and Ph. D. degrees in Applied Mathematics from Indian Institute of Technology (Indian School of Mines) Dhanbad in the year 2007 and 2011, respectively. He is the recipient of University Gold Medal in his Masters. Dr. Nandkeolyar has guided 08 scholars for their Ph. D. degrees and 15 Students for their Master's Dissertation. Dr. Nandkeolyar has published a number of research papers in reputed SCI/SCIE listed international journals. His research interests include theoretical fluid flow modeling along stretching surfaces, nanofluid flows, and flow along curved surfaces. Dr. Nandkeolyar has successfully executed a research project funded by Science & Engineering Research Board (Department of Science & Technology), Government of India. One more research project funded by SERB is ongoing. Dr. Nandkeolyar is the lead member of the Project Implementation Group (PIG) for the FIST support received by the Department of Mathematics, NIT Jamshedpur.  His teaching interests include Numerical Analysis, Fluid Dynamics, Ordinary Differential Equations and Integral Transforms.
Research Interests:
Fluid Dynamics:
Investigation of hydrodynamic problems over different geometries, study of impact of various factors on the boundary layers, skin-friction and heat transfer coefficients, fluid flow involving nanofluids.
Magnetohydrodynamics:
Study of the flow of viscous, incompressible, electrically conducting fluids under the influence of magnetic fields over different geometries, heat transfer phenomena, stability analysis of magnetohydrodynamic problems.
Numerical Analysis:
Development of spectral based numerical methods for the solution of hydrodynamic and hydromagnetic problems.
Major Research Projects:
Modelling & Simulation of Three-Dimensional Magnetohydrodynamic Nanofluid flows over a Stretching Surface
(ECR/2017/000118) funded by Science and Engineering Research Board under ECRA Scheme.
Magnetohydrodynamics of Hybrid Nanofluids with Dissipative Heat Transfer: Non-similar Analysis
(MTR/2021/000426) funder by Science and Engineering Research Board under MATRICS Scheme.
Lead Member of the Project Investigator Group (PIG) for FIST Support awarded to Department of Mathematics, NIT Jamshedpur

Dr Rajat Tripathi
Assistant Professor
Department Of Mathematics
I have been working at NIT Jamshedpur Since June 2018 as an Assistant Professor in the Department of Mathematics. Before Joining NIT Jamshedpur I worked as an Assistant Professor at REC Rewa from January 2018 to May 2018. Before starting my career as an Assistant Professor, I enrolled for a PhD degree at Indian Institute of Technology (ISM) Dhanbad in March 2013 and earned my doctoral degree in September 2017. For my PhD, I worked on some problems of Magnetohydrodynamics, which is a sub branch of Fluid Dynamics. At NIT Jamshedpur, I have been involved in teaching at undergraduate and postgraduate levels and continuing my research work on t
he problems of Magnetohydrodynamics, Thin film flows and electroosmosis. Under my supervision, 3 students have earned their PhD degrees and at present 3 research students are working with me for their Doctoral degree. I am also part of a project implementation group which secured a funding of
Rs. 8 Millions under FIST scheme
of DST (GOI) to develope a Scientific Computing laboratory and a library at Department of Mathematics. Apart from teaching Mathematics and doing research, I am involved in heading some extracurricular activities of students. FACES (Fine Arts Club of Engineering Students) is one such place where students get to showcase their talents in fine arts, organization of events for students of institute as well as kids from nearby schools.

Dr Ram Krishna
Assistant Professor
Metallurgical and Materials Engineering
PhD: Mechanics of Materials, School of Engineering, The University of Leicester, Leicester, United Kingdom.
M.Tech: Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur, India.
B.Tech: National Institute of Technology, Jamshedpur, India.
Postdoctoral Research Fellow: North Carolina State University, Raleigh, North Carolina, USA/Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Oak Ridge, TN, USA/Idaho National Laboratory, Idaho Falls, ID, USA/ University of Wisconsin–Madison, WI, USA.
Research Experience: The University of Manchester, Manchester, United Kingdom/EDF Energy Generation/NNL, United Kingdom (UK National Laboratory for Nuclear Science)/Diamond Light Source (UK's national synchrotron science facility), Oxford, United Kingdom/SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory - Stanford University, Sand Hill Rd, Menlo Park, CA, USA.
Dr Ram Krishna is an experienced metals researcher and academic with a background in metallurgy. He received his Bachelor of Engineering degree in metallurgical engineering and material science from the National Institute of Technology (NIT), Jamshedpur, and his Master's degree in materials and metallurgical engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur. Dr Krishna continued his studies at the University of Leicester, UK, obtaining his PhD in 2011. He has held postdoctoral positions at the University of Manchester, UK and North Carolina State University, USA. His research interests cover many materials for high-temperature applications, including mechanical testing of their behaviour and performance and advanced characterisation techniques, as evidenced by his H-index of 14 and 2 utility patents under examination. He has authored or co-authored more than 52 research papers in international journals and conference proceedings. His current research focuses on 3D printing of metallic and ceramic alloys and materials for 3D printing applications.

Dr Ravi Bhushan
Assistant Professor
Electrical Engineering
Dr. Ravi Bhushan received his B. Sc. Engineering degree in Electrical
Engineering, in 2009 from the Bhagalpur College of Engineering, Bhagalpur,
India. He received his M. Tech. degree in Power Systems (Department of
Electrical Engineering), in 2011 from IIT BHU, Varanasi, India. From July,
2011 to Jan 2014, he worked as an assistant professor in the Department of
Electrical Engineering, HITM Agra (SGI), India. In March 2018, he
completed his Ph. D. degree from IIT (ISM) Dhanbad, Jharkhand, India. He
is presently working as an Assistant Professor (Grade-I) in the Department of Electrical
Engineering, NIT Jamshedpur, Jharkhand, India since Sept. 2022. He served as an Assistant Professor (Grade-II)  from Oct. 2018 to Sept. 2022 in the Department of Electrical
Engineering, NIT Srinagar, J&K, India. He also worked as an Assistant Professor from Sept. 2017 to Sept. 2018 in the Department of Electrical
Engineering, NIT Patna, Bihar, India. His research interests include Power System Stability and control, Renewable Energy Systems, and Optimal Control. He has
taken many expert lectures throughout the country and published many
international research articles of repute. He has been member for several
Selection Committee and Active member of many professional bodies, such
as IEEE (USA), Institute of Engineers (India), ISTE, International
Association of Engineers (IAENG) etc. He is reviewer of many reputed
journals and conferences. In addition, he is currently Guest Editor of
Distributed Generation & Alternative Energy Journal.

Prof Satish Kumar
Professor
Mechanical Engineering
Dr. Satish Kumar is presently working as a Professor
in the Department of Mechanical Engineering, National Institute of Technology
Jamshedpur. He has more than 21 years of Teaching and Research experience. Dr.
Satish Kumar obtained his bachelor’s and Master degree from Department of
Mechanical Engineering, SVNIT Surat, in 2002 and 2004. He has completed his
Ph.D.
under the supervision of Professor
B. K. Gandhi,
Department
of Mechanical and Industrial Engineering, IIT Roorkee in the area of solid –
liquid flow in 2014.
His research
interests are, Rheology of Slurry Flow, Computational Fluid Dynamics, Erosion
Wear, Flow Phenomena of Solid-Liquid Flow in Pump and Pipeline. He authored
(and co-authored) over 176 research articles including 90 in SCI Index journals
in the field of multiphase flow. He has the Editor of the many reputed journals
and books. He supervised 16 Ph.D. and
55 M
. Tech Thesis in the area of Multiphase
flow. Dr. Satish Kumar . Google scholar H –Index- is 33, H 10
Index is 159
and Scopus H –Index is 28.
Prof.
Satish Kumar is currently working as Dean Research & Consultancy, Nodal
officer Research Innovation Park
.
He is looking the NIRF activity
of institute as Chainman & Nodal officer, NIRF
.
He
was also hold the
Faculty In-charge Admission, Controller of Examination
from 2020 to 2023,
Chairman of Institute
Publication Cell, Chairman of
Institute
News-letter from 2019 to 2023
at
NIT Jamshedpur. Currently supervising 06 Ph.D.
students He has organized two national conferences, two international conferences,
Two Science and Engineering Research Board SERB sponsored high end Karyshala,
two ATAL-AICTE sponsored Faculty development program and more than 16 faculty
development programme/ short term courses.
He has completed 07 sponsored research project funded
by different agencies like SERB,
DST
, UGC successfully. Currently, 04 research
projects is ongoing. He is a life member of ISTE, ASME, NSFMFP, IAENG,
Institution of Engineers, NITTSD etc.
He
has listed in top 2% world scientist as surveyed by Stanford University.

Prof Shashi Bhushan  Prasad
Professor
Production and Industrial Engineering
Dr. Shashi Bhushan Prasad is working as
        a Professor in Department of Production and Industrial Engineering,
        National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur.
He has more
        than 27 years of teaching experience. His area of interests are Energy, Energy
        Management, Production Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Welding Technology,
        etc. He is a faculty in National Institute of Technology, Jamshedpur since 27
th
March 1998. He was a faculty in Govt. Polytechnic, Latehar from August 1996 to March
        1998. He graduated in Mechanical Engineering from MIT Muzaffaupur in 1991 and completed
        his M. Tech in Machine Design from NIT Jamshedpur erstwhile, RIT Jamshedpur in
        2002. He has been awarded Ph. D Degree in Mechanical and Industrial Engineering
        Department, IIT Roorkee in 2009. He was also a National Merit Scholarship holder
        during his high school, Intermediate and Graduation period. He has authored
        (and co-authored) over 45 research articles in peer reviewed journals, book
        chapters and conferences. He has supervised 09 Ph.D. out of which 4 has been
        awarded and 02 has been submitted and 15 MTech Thesis. He has completed a
        research project sponsored by NID successfully. He is the Life member ISTE
        and fellow member of Institution of Engineers.

Dr Shubham Tripathi
Assistant Professor
Production and Industrial Engineering
I joined NIT Jamshedpur as an  Assistant Professor in Production & Industrial Engineering Department in September 2022. I have handled subjects including Supply Chain Management, operations research, measurement and metrology, business statistics, introduction to machine learning and Industrial Economics for undergraduates and operations research for Masters and PhD students. Prior to this assignment, I have worked in Mechanical Engineering Department, NIT Goa from August, 2021 to June, 2022. I taught several subjects including Industrial Engineering and Operations Research, Production and Operations Management, Supply Chain Management and Manufacturing Processes to undergraduates at NIT Goa. I earned my Doctorate in November, 2021 from MNNIT Allahabad where I enrolled for the degree in July 2017. My research area in  PhD was Supply Chain Management. My PhD thesis focused at facilitating the transformation of Indian supply chains in view of fourth Industrial revolution. I obtained my Masters in Technology from Production & Industrial Engineering Department, NIT Jalandhar in 2017 where I was awarded Gold Medal for the 2015-17 batch. My M. tech project focused on Inventory management an Demand forecasting and I interned with a valve manufacturing firm during 2nd year for the project. I received Emerging Young Scientist Award from Society for Science and Nature in 2018.

Dr Mondal’s prime research interests are thermal characterization of geomaterials, utilization of industrial by-products, energy geotechnics, heat induced moisture migration, thermo-hydro-mechanical behaviour of clay
.

Assistant Professor

Dr Subrata Mahanta
Assistant Professor
Department of Chemistry
Dr. Subrata Mahanta is currently working as an assistant professor at the department of Chemistry, NIT Jamshedpur.
After finishing his masters from the University of Calcutta and clearings CSIR-JRF NET, he joined as a PhD scholar at Calcutta University under the supervision of Prof. Nikhil Guchhait and Prof. Deb Narayan Nath of IACS, Kolkata (co-supervisor). His thesis title was “Photo-induced Processes of Some Organic Molecules: Fluorescence Spectroscopy and Quantum Chemical Calculation”. His research works during his PhD tenure was mainly in studying the fundamental photophysical properties or activities of self-designed and synthesized molecules. Moreover, he also studied the photophysical behaviors of these molecules in the confined mediums such as micelles, reverse micelles, protein environments e.g. HSA and BSA and cyclodextrine.
After finishing his PhD, he went to the department of Bimolecular Optics (BMO), Ludwig Maximilians University (LMU), Munich, Germany to pursue his first postdoctoral research in Prof. Dr. Eberhard Riedle’s group. He was an Alexander von Humboldt(AvH) postdoctoral fellow in this lab from April 2009 to March 2011.
After finishing his first postdoctoral research in Germany then he moved to Japan  as a postdoctoral fellow at national institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST)-Tsukuba, Japan in Dr. Akihiro Furube’s group.  Here at AIST, he  studied the interfacial electron transfer or more clearly on electron injection efficiency of dye sensitized solar cells (DSSCs) using femtosecond as well as sub-nanosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, time correlated single photon counting (TCSPC), Streak Camera methods.
Currently he is doing research on molecular spectroscopy, biophysical (DNA intercalations, Protein-Probe interactions, Drug design etc.), theoretical chemistry and environmental science.

Dr Sudhanshu Shekhar Pati
Assistant Professor
Department of Chemistry
Dr. Pati is an Assistant Professor in the Department of Chemistry, National Institute of Technology, Jamshedpur. He received his PhD degree from Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research, Kalpakkam in 2014. Later, he joined as a postdoc in Universidade de Brasília, Brazil and IIT, Kharagpur for about 2 years before joining NIT, Jamshedpur. His research focuses on Nanomaterials (Magnetic and Non-magnetic) synthesis which can be effortlessly manipulated by external stimuli. The target applications of the prepared nanomaterials include Water Treatment, Magnetic Hyperthermia and Energy Storage.

Dr Sumit Kumar Debnath
Assistant Professor
Department Of Mathematics
Sumit Kumar Debnath is an Assistant Professor (Grade-I) in the Department of Mathematics, National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur, India. He received his doctoral
degree in cryptology & network security from the Indian Institute of Technology
Kharagpur, India, in 2017. He has published several research articles in internationally reputed journals and conferences. He is PI of several National and International research projects. He is a life member of the Cryptology Research Society of India (CRSI). His research interests include post-quantum cryptography, quantum cryptography, secure two-party/multi-party computation, secure set intersection, electronic
voting, blockchain technology, functional encryption, identity-based cryptography, and oblivious transfer.

Dr Surajit Kundu
Assistant Professor
Electronics and Communication Engineering
Surajit Kundu
(SMIEEE, SMURSI) received his B. Tech degree in Electronics
and Communication Engineering in 2009, M. Tech degree from the Dept. of E&ECE, Indian Institute of
Technology Kharagpur in 2012 and Ph. D. degree from National Institute of
Technology Sikkim in 2018. He served UIT, The University of Burdwan in the year of
2013 as an Assistant Professor. He worked as an Assistant Professor in the
Department of ECE, NIT Sikkim from 2014 to 2022. Presently he is serving the
Dept. of ECE, NIT Jamshedpur as Assistant Professor (Grade-1). His research
interests include Antenna Engineering, IoT, Satellite Communication and Navigation, 5G and beyond wireless technology, Ground
Penetrating Radar, Frequency Selective Surfaces, Metasurfaces. He published 86 research
papers in SCI journals and conference proceedings. He received the “Young
Indian Radio Scientist” award from URSI in New Delhi, India during AP-RASC-2019. He
won best paper award in NERC 2022, I3C-20 and many more conferences. Presently
he is the senior member of IEEE and senior member of URSI. He served as Associate
editor and regular reviewer of many reputed journals. He was
identified as top 2% most influential Scientists (single year) in 2023
and 2024 by Stanford University. He completed or
carrying several projects from various Indian Government sponsoring agencies
such as ANRF, DST, TEXMIN, HEFA, TEQIP etc. in capacity of Principal
Investigator. He conducted Eight Workshop/Short Term Course/ Skill Development
Training programmes as Coordinator which were funded by IEEE, MSME, AICTE, SERB,
DST, TEQIP etc.

Dr Sushil Kumar Gupta
Associate Professor
Electrical Engineering
Dr. Sushil Kumar Gupta is an
Associate Professor and the Head of the Electrical Engineering Department at
the National Institute of Technology (NIT) Jamshedpur. He obtained his Bachelor
of Science in Engineering (B.Sc. Engg) in Electrical Engineering from MIT
Muzaffarpur in 1985, and he completed his Master of Technology (M.Tech) in
Power System Engineering at NIT Jamshedpur in 1988. He earned his Ph.D. from
NIT Jamshedpur in April 2023, further enhancing his expertise in power systems.
Dr. Gupta began his academic career as an Assistant Professor in the Electrical
Engineering Department at GBPUAT, Pant Nagar, from July 1987 to August 1988. He
then joined NIT Jamshedpur (previously called RIT Jamshedpur) as a Lecturer in
August 1988, was selected as an Assistant Professor in March 1996, and was
promoted to Associate Professor on January 1, 2006. With over 36 years of
teaching experience, Dr. Gupta has made significant contributions to the
academic community, focusing on power systems research, mentoring students, and
advancing his field. As the Head of the Electrical Engineering Department, he
continues to promote academic excellence and foster innovation in power systems
at NIT Jamshedpur.

Dr. Tushar Banerjee is currently working in the post of Assistant Professor (Grade-I) at Department of Production & Industrial Engineering. He obtained his
PhD from Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur (2017), Master of Engineering in Mechanical Engineering from Jadavpur University, Kolkata (2011) and Bachelor of Engineering in Mechanical Engineering from National Institute of Technology Agartala (2008).

Dr Veerpratap Meena
Assistant Professor
Electrical Engineering
Dr. Veerpratap Meena
(M’21, IEEE) is an
Assistant Professor in the Department of Electrical Engineering at the National Institute of Technology (NIT), Jamshedpur, India
. He received his B.Tech. degree in Electrical Engineering from Govt. Engineering College, Bikaner, in 2018, followed by an M.Tech. in Power System Engineering from the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Roorkee in 2020. He completed his Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering at Malaviya National Institute of Technology (MNIT), Jaipur, in 2023, and a postdoctoral fellowship at Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Bengaluru, in 2024. Dr. Meena has been actively involved in IEEE, serving as the Chair of the IEEE Systems Council Systems Education Technical Committee, USA, since 2023. He also holds leadership roles in the IEEE Delhi Section and Rajasthan Subsection, including Chair of the IEEE Delhi Section-Rajasthan Aerospace and Electronic Systems Society Chapter and the IEEE Systems Council Joint Section Chapter. His research focuses on Microgrids, Renewable Energy, Power Electronics, Optimization, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Smart Grids, Net-Zero Energy Grids, Electric Vehicles, Control Systems, Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading, and Healthcare. He has published extensively in leading international journals and conferences and serves as an Associate Editor for IEEE ACCESS, e-Prime: Advances in Electrical Engineering, Electronics and Energy, Discover Applied Sciences, and other reputed journals.
Dr. Meena is actively involved in organizing international IEEE conferences and technical events. He has served as General Chair, Program Chair, Special Session Organizer, and Technical Program Committee Member for several prestigious conferences. He has organized special sessions at renowned conferences, including IECON, ISIE, AUPEC, SGRE, ICIT, SYSCON, GPECOM, CPE-PowerEng, IAS Annual Meetings, and others. As a keynote speaker, he has delivered expert talks at various global conferences, sharing insights on advanced topics in electrical engineering and smart energy systems. In 2024, he was recognized among the
world’s top 2% of scientists by Stanford University and Elsevier
for his contributions to research. Dr. Meena continues to drive innovation through his research, academic leadership, and active participation in global scientific communities.

Dr Vijay Kumar Dalla
Assistant Professor

PhD in Space Robotics (2016) from IIT Roorkee
MTech in Materials Science (2008) from IIT Bombay

Dr. Vijay Kumar Dalla is an esteemed Assistant Professor (Grade-I) in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at NIT Jamshedpur, serving since May 23, 2018. With a distinguished academic and research background, his expertise spans robotics, dynamics, and control.
Dr. Dalla earned his Ph.D. in Robotics from IIT Roorkee in 2016, following a Bachelor of Engineering (B.E.) in Mechanical Engineering from Government Engineering College, Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh in 2006. He holds an M.Tech in Materials Science from IIT Bombay (2008). With a rich academic exposure of seven years across two IITs and over a decade of teaching experience, Dr. Dalla has significantly contributed to advancing knowledge in robotics & automation, kinematics, dynamics, and control of mechanical systems, AI in robotics. His research focuses on space robotics, dynamics, and control, and he has also gained hands-on experience in fracture mechanics, materials science, and ceramic powder processing.
A prolific researcher, Dr. Dalla has published 30 research papers in reputed international journals and conferences, and three book chapters.
He has successfully supervised one Ph.D. scholar and is currently guiding four doctoral students. His commitment to academic excellence is further reflected in his active involvement in outreach initiatives, faculty development programs (FDPs), and workshops. Dr. Dalla is a lifetime member of The Association for Machines and Mechanisms (AMM) and The Robotics Society.
His dedication to innovation is evident in his role as Principal Investigator for two ongoing funded robotics projects from TiHaN-IITH and IIT Guwahati Technology Innovation and Development Foundation, with a total grant of ₹32 lakhs. Earlier in his career, he was associated with two BRNS projects during his tenure as a Senior Research Fellow at IIT Bombay.
With a relentless passion for developing application-driven robotic systems, Dr. Dalla continues to push the boundaries of robotics research, shaping the future of intelligent and autonomous systems.

Dr Vineet Sahoo
Assistant Professor
Mechanical Engineering
Dr. Vineet
Sahoo has completed his PhD from Indian Institute of Technology (IIT)
Kharagpur, India, where he carried out his research work under Prof Rathindranath
Maiti's supervision. He received his bachelor's degree in Mechanical
Engineering in 2006 from Utkal University Orissa and Master's degree in
Mechanical System Design in 2012 from IIT Kharagpur.
My PhD thesis
work focused on estimation of static load sharing in involute internal-external
gear set. An analytical solution is proposed for the estimation. From a
standard rim thickness gear to thin rim gears are considered to observe the
variation in load sharing. The study is further extended to harmonic drive.
Harmonic drive is a high-speed reduction unit in a compact space. Robot joints
(including precision medical robots, solar panel/radar position control devices
in general and in space vehicles/stations, computer printer roller drives,
active front wheel steering mechanism of Audi, are few of its application
examples. In support of the amount static load sharing in harmonic drive,
experimental investigation and finite element simulation in ANSYS is carried
out. During my research work, I acquired very good hands-on software like Solidworks
modeling, Auto-cad, ANSYS (FEM toolbox). I developed my skills to put logics in
MATLAB programming for analytical solutions. I have become more interested in
experiments, as the whole setup (except harmonic drive unit) is developed in
the laboratory. Besides my PhD research work, I have also worked on gear pump,
where I did the geometrical analysis on entrapped volume and its effect on gear
tooth deflections through FEM. Recently, I am also working on high temperature
superconducting cable and variable clearance bearing design. Based on research
field, eleven journal papers and nine conference papers were published.
Recently PI is sanctioned with DST Indo-serbia Joint project 2022 on “
Development of Zero Backlash Power
Transmission Mechanism for Anthropomorphic Robots”

Dr Vishesh Ranjan Kar
Assistant Professor
Mechanical Engineering
Dr. Kar is presently working as Assistant Professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering, National Institute of Technology Jamshedpur, India, since 2018. He has over 15 years of teaching, research and industrial experience. He received his doctoral degree from NIT Rourkela in 2015 under the guidance of Prof. S. K. Panda in the field of Computational Solid Mechanics. His research interests are Nonlinear Finite Element Method, Advanced Composite Structures, Computational Mechanics and Shape Optimization. So far, he authored (and co-authored) over 110 research articles in peer-reviewed journals, books and conferences in the field of modeling and analysis of composite structures. He is also the Editorial Board Member of the Journal of the Mechanical Behavior of Materials,  the Achieves  of Advanced Engineering Science, and Green Nanotechnology. He has handled and also handling various research projects as Principal Investigator (and Co-PI) funded by government and private agencies. He already guided 05 PhD thesis and also presently guiding 06 PhD students. He is the recipient of Research Award 2016 from VIT University, Vellore, India; Early Career Research Award 2017 from Department of Science & Technology, Government of India, and also received Young Scientist and Researcher Awards from various National and International agencies. He has been recognized as one of the Top 2% Scientists in the World, published in  Elsevier by Stanford University for year 2021, 2022 and 2023.  He also portrait in Who’s Who in Engineering Higher Education and Shell Buckling People. He is a recognized reviewer for many reputed international journals in the field of analysis of composite structures. He is a life-time member of Indian Society for Applied Mechanics, Institute of Engineers (India), and few other national and international engineering societies.
Apart from teaching and research activities, he has been involved in various administration activities. He served as Associate Dean (Research & Consultancy) from 2020-2022, and presently holding the position of Associate Dean (Academic: Recognition & Accreditation).

Prof. Ram Vinoy Sharma
Deputy Director
Prof Ram Vinoy Sharma is currently the Deputy Director of N.I.T Jamshedpur. He earned his B.E. degree from Indian Institute of Technology Delhi in 1985 and his M.E. from Indian Institute of Technology Delhi in 1987. He completed his PhD from Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur in 1999. He is the professor of Department of Mechanical Engineering, N.I.T. Jamshedpur from 1st Jan. 2008.

Academics
NIT Jamshedpur is a prestigious institute of higher learning producing meritorious students with excellent career growth and universal recognition. The students get the best of opportunities in the form of highly advanced courses and eminent faculty members.The institute is committed to academic excellence and good governance. NIT Jamshedpur was ranked overall 78th for 2015-16, 79th in 2020, 86th in 2021 and 90th in 2022 among the best 100 engineering institutes in the country by the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) for higher education institutions released by the Ministry of Education, Government of India. Admission Policy
The Institute adopts the MHRD, Government of India guidelines for admission to all academic programmes of the Institute.
UG
The admission to the under graduate programmes is made on the performance in the class 12/equivalent qualifying examination and in the JEE (Main). The Joint Seat Allocation Authority (JoSAA) / Central Seat Allocation Board (CSAB) allocates the seats for Under Graduate Programmes through Common Counseling process.For general guidelines of B.Tech Admissions and documents required,
Click Here
M.Tech
M. Tech. students are admitted on the basis of their GATE score & seat distribution according to Centralized Counselling for M.Tech./M.Arch./M.Plan. Admissions(CCMT). For Online Registration Form and other information of CCMT,
Click Here
M.Sc.
The admission to M.Sc. Programmes is based on JAM Score in the JAM examination and through Centralized Counseling for M.Sc. (CCMN).For admission procedure,
Click Here
MCA
The admission to MCA Programme is based on NIT MCA Common Entrance Test (NIMCET) examination jointly conducted by NITs and through centralized common counseling. For Online Registration Form and other information of NIMCET ,
Click Here
PhD
The admission to PhD programme is through direct notification given by the institute. The selection of the candidates are made on the basis of tests/interview conducted by the respective departments.For general guidelines of PhD Admissions and documents required,
Click Here

Health and Welfare
To cater the medical needs of the employees and students, the institute has round the clock medical facilities at Institute Health Centre as well as in the empanelled hospitals/nursing homes in the city. It is being monitored by a medical services committee.
Institute Health Center (Dispensary)
Provides treatment for basic day-to-day health problems (minor ailments) and medicines to employees, their dependents and students.
The dispensary has following staffs:-
1. Dr. Abhay Kumar- Medical Officer
2. Dr. Aakanksha Sumedha- Medical Officer
3. K. P. Dubey - Medical Assistant-1
4. Kanchan Devi - Attendant
5. Motilal Gaur - Caretaker
Treatment at Empanneled Hospitals in city
In case of the employees and their dependents who need treatment from specialists, they can get treatment in any five empanelled hospitals, on cashless basis, namely
1. Tata Main Hospital, Jamshedpur
3. Brahmananda Hospital, Jamshedpur
4. A.S.G. Eye Hospital, Jamshedpur
5. Rajasthan Sewa Sadan Hospital, Jamshedpur
The medicines prescribed by the doctors are also provided to them from empanelled shops on cashless basis.
Pathological Facility
Aarogyam Pathology Laboratory
Adityapur is empanelled for various pathological tests on cashless basis for the employee and their dependents.
Medical Facilities to Students
The students are also provided Emergency and Inside admission medical facilities on cashless basis in Tata Main Hospital, Bistupur and OPD facility in Steel City Hospital, Bistupur through Medical Insurance. Other than this, in case of emergency, they can get themselves treated in any of the Hospitals/Nursing homes in Jamshedpur as well as other hospitals in country and the medical expenses incurred by them is reimbursed through insurance.
Referral Cases
Employees and their dependents can get referred to any higher centres in the country on the recommendation of the hospitals.
Visiting Specialised Doctors
The arrangement is also done for providing the services of specialist doctors of a particular specialization to the employees and students on cashless basis in the Institute health centre.
Ambulance Facility
Ambulance facility is available 24*7 for emergency needs of both the staff and students.

Campus Life
You have worked hard enough to get in to NIT. Now it is time to ease your loads, enjoy the reward and involve yourself in interesting activities to develop your personality and sharpen your skills. There is a whole lot of activities of various clubs and teams going on in the institute to keep you busy for the entire year.
We have classes from 8am to 5 pm during weekdays, while weekends are left for you to enjoy, relax and study too!!! In your first odd semester, by the time you get used to the institute life you will find yourself working alongside different clubs. In the meantime you will be facing tests, assignments, quizzes and the mighty-end sems.
But no need to panic as the time passes so fast that you won’t even realize when your semester is over. When you come back in even sem you will be watching and taking part in the fests of the institute like sports meet, Culfest and Ojass.
And if you l like going out you can always visit the beautiful city of Jamshedpur. Some of the major tourist attractions of the city are Jubilee park which was a gift by Tata Steel to the citizens of Jamshedpur on the completion of its 50 years. Dimna Lake is an artificial reservoir and one of the main sources for the city's drinking water. Dalma Hills are north of the Subarnarenkha river, they stretch 16 km from east to west. The other important ones are Tata Steel Zoological Park, Chandil Dam, Rivers Meet, Hudco Lake, Centre for Excellence (CE), Sir Dorabji Tata Park, Moolgaokar Park, Bhuvneswari Temple and others.

No Ragging
Does the mention of the word ragging give you goose-bumps and make you break into a sweat? Ragging, in NIT jamshedpur, is strictly forbidden. You may be ling a little bit overwhelmed at the prospect of living in a hostel without your parents, but, rest assured, you, just like we did, will meet cheerful and helpful seniors at your hostel’s help desk the day you and your parents arrive. 1. STUDENTS’ COUNCIL
Students’ Council will be the highest governing body of Students Activities Centre and will be responsible for all the Students Activities taking place in the Institute.
1.1 Objective
A good administration and efficient students’ council is a part of an able institution. Students’ Council represents the opinions, ideas and proposals of the students.
To provide a link and improve communication between administration, students and parents.
To provide a forum for students to voice their opinions on relevant issues.
To encourage students to become self-confident, responsible and create a more caring atmosphere.
The Council functions to bridge the gap between students and administration, paving way to the healthy relationship between the two, thereby creating a conducive environment for their Academic and extracurricular excellence .
The administration is more approachable through the council, and also the demands and problems faced by the students are given a patient ear.
To maintain transparency in all types of students activities in the institute.
This document provides the Students’ Council with an explanation of its purpose, administration and responsibilities. Students’ Council should be notified before any decision is made.
1.2  Structure of Students’ Council
The students’ council of National Institute of Technology, Jamshedpur comprises of the following posts whose eligibility criteria are mentioned in the selection procedure as notified by the institute.
1. President (4th year B.Tech.)
2. Vice-President (3rd year B.Tech.)

One of the attractions of this campus is the OVAL structure - the Computer Centre, which accommodates central computing facilities. There are mainly three types of services viz. computational services, laboratory services and network services. The Centre's services are extensively used by the students, faculty and staff members of the Institute. The centre is equipped with IBM Servers(2), Dell-EMC Servers(4), HP Server(1) and Lenovo tower Server(1). Various systems and application softwares are installed and maintained by the centre. There are eight Computer-Laboratories, which are used for UG/PG classes and one for Internet services. The internet service is available through two Leased line(L1.1  1Gbps & L1.1 2 Gbps) on all week days from 08 :00 AM to 10 :00 PM. The network services are limited to the centre, but it is to be extended to the whole academic and residential campus shortly. The floor space of the centre is being augmented in order to accommodate a Multimedia Laboratory, a CAD Laboratory, and a Smart Seminar Room. In a CAD Laboratory mainly consists of following Softwares:- Solid works, Ansys, AutoCad & Fest (ISRO sponsored).

The Committee's Function:
1.
Conduct a prompt and impartial investigation into the incident.
2.
Establish clear and confidential reporting mechanisms for incidents of harassment.
3.
Ensure the victim's safety and well-being are prioritized.
4.
To take proactive steps to raise awareness of gender issues among NIT Jamshedpur's teachers, staff, and students.
5.
Promote a culture of respect and accountability within the institution.
6.
To fulfill any additional responsibilities as outlined by the act.
Women at work place: Working without Harassment
According to the Supreme Court, sexual harassment comprises the following behaviours: making advances or physical contact
1.
Demanding or requesting sexual favours
2.
Making sexually suggestive comments
3.
Displaying pornography
4.
Engaging in any other unwanted physical, verbal, or nonverbal behaviour of a sexual character.
What steps should you take if you encounter sexual harassment?
1.
Do not experience guilt. Make it extremely apparent to the harasser that you find his actions insulting
2.
Keep in mind that harassment will not end on its own if you choose to ignore it. Inform the Internal Complaints Committee of your grievances by coming forward.
3.
Document every instance of sexual harassment. This record will be useful if you ever feel the need to file a formal complaint.
4.
Engaging in any other unwanted physical, verbal, or nonverbal behaviour of a sexual character.
Who can approach ICC and file a complaint?
Any woman employee (faculty and staff including contractual, casual and temporary) of NIT Jamshedpur, female students, and any women residing in NIT Jamshedpur Campus or visiting the Campus in any capacity may file a complaint against an incident of sexual harassment.
How and where to file a complaint?
The person concerned can personally approach/telephone/write/e-mail to any member of ICC followed by the submission of a formal written complaint as a hard copy addressed to the Presiding Officer, ICC within 90 days of the incident about which the complaint is filed. The ICC is required to complete the process of inquiry and submit its report within 90 days of the filing of the complaint. The formal complaint must contain the following:
Register your Complaint here
The formal complaint must contain the following:
- Date and time of the incident
- The place where it occurred
- Name and contact information of the accused
- Name and contact information of witnesses
- Detailed description of the incident

"Everything that you need for better future and success has already been written. And guess what? All you have to do is go to the Library." The Central Library came into existence as an important component of the institute in 1960. It continues to provide the following categories of services to its users : Students, Teachers, Researchers and other staff members.
Routine transaction (lending and retrieval) of books
Providing Reference materials
Reprographic services
Reading room services
Space
The three storied Library premises are situated adjacent to the Administrative Block of the Institute. It spans a total floor space of about 32,184 sq. t, consisting of a separate Reading Hall, Periodical section, a processing section, stack Room, Book Bank and a Binding Unit, as briefly described below.
Reading Room:
It is situated in the ground floor. It stores Encyclopedias, Dictionaries, Handbooks, News papers, popular Magazines, Journal & Reference Books for on the spot use of the Library users.:
Stack Room
It is situated in the ground floor. It stores Encyclopedias, Dictionaries, Handbooks, News papers, popular Magazines, Journal & Reference Books for on the spot use of the Library users.:
Book Bank
There are two Book Banks in the Library.
One of them is meant for the students belonging to scheduled cast (SC) & Scheduled Tribe (ST). It was established under a scheme sanctioned by the government of Bihar (Welfare Department). Under this scheme the Welfare department, earlier Bihar Govt. but now Jharkhand Government, through their Disctrict Welfare Officer, supplies books & Almirahs. As many as 15 books are issued for one academic session to a SC /ST student from such a Book Bank.
The other Book Bank is TEQIP Book Bank, used by both SC/ST students and General students. TEQIP Book Bank is governed & funded by World Bank Aid. Two Books are issued from this Book Bank for one academic session to a student. Recently new chairs and tables have been purchased through TEQIP-II fund.
Acquisition & Processing Unit
This is situated on the top floor on the library. New arrivals of Books & Journals are processed. (Accessioning, Cataloguing & Classification) here before they are stocked in the stack room.
New arrivals of Books during 2006-2013.
Books of different titles were purchased for both the Book Banks during this year, comprising of a total of 35,000 Books.

Other Facilities
The Library subscribes to a sizeable number of technical, scientific & general periodicals journal & newspapers for the students and faculty members of the Institute. The Library system is ready to shift from manual to automated system, which include circulation, serial & online public access catalogue (OPAC) searching. Tender for Data entry work of the books will be out soon, and thereafter linking of Circulation Deptt is to be done (issue & return of books, books position and up-to-date information regarding any book) in order to make the Library user friendly. A Book Scanner has been employed in the Central Library for the same. To match the pace of the digital world, the Library has purchased the latest version of LIBNET software 7.0.
In addition to this we have online service through INDEST CONSORTIUM on the subjects for the following:

Moreover the Library has subscribed for J-Gate subscription and is going to subscribe IEEE journals very soon. A subscription of ebooks from TMH amounting to Rs 34lacs and purchase of books (in print version) is in line. Thereafter, ten newspapers and magazines will be subscribed by the Library.

Filing of RTI Application Form
A person seeking information may file an application on form either in writing or by e-mail giving particulars of the information being sought.
The application along with the requisite  can be submitted in the form of Cash/Demand Draft/Bankers' Cheque. Demand Draft/Bankers' Cheque can be sent in favour of 'Director, National Institute of Technology, Jamshedpur' payable at SBI, RIT Campus Branch, Jamshedpur, 831014.
In case request is made by e-mail, the  should be deposited within seven days. Non-receipt of  will imply withdrawal of request.
Important Information
The Institute will endeavor to provide the information sought within 30 days upon payment of the requisite fees.
The time limit of providing information concerning life and liberty of a person is 48 hours.
In case the information pertains to a third party, the time limit is 40 days.
If no reply or information is received as above, it is deemed to have been rejected. The applicant will be intimated the reasons for rejection.
